choices.text: Configure Aurora Auto Scaling and send aggregation SQL to the existing writer endpoint as well
choices.explanation: Adding replicas does not move the aggregation load sent to the writer.

choices.text: Pool SQL connections to the writer with RDS Proxy and send all SQL to the same writer
choices.explanation: This reduces connection-management overhead, but query execution load remains on the writer and it does not automatically scale replicas.

choices.text: Pin all clients to the reader's instance endpoint
choices.explanation: New connections cannot be distributed to replicas added later.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Increasing the number of replicas alone does not move existing SQL directed to the writer.
learning.concept: Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts the number of read replicas. The reader endpoint distributes new connections, so SQL is not spread across replicas when clients keep using one long-lived connection.

check.prompt: Why might aggregation be concentrated on one instance even when there are four replicas?
check.answer: The aggregation pool may keep using the same connection. Check the connection lifetime and number of connections.

title: Caching for a Frequently Updated API
prompt: Some SKUs receive a high concentration of reads through an inventory lookup API. Updates are committed in RDS, and the tolerated read delay is at most 30 seconds. The API must continue retrieving data from the source database if the cache is empty or unavailable. Which design should you adopt?

choices.text: Use a local cache on each EC2 instance with no expiration
choices.explanation: Updates do not propagate to other nodes, so this cannot meet the short delay requirement.

choices.text: Use an RDS Proxy connection pool and run the same lookup against RDS every time
choices.explanation: This improves connection management but does not reduce SQL reads for the same SKU.

choices.text: Write updates to ElastiCache first, then write them back to RDS in batches every minute
choices.explanation: If the cache fails before the write-back, an update that appeared committed could be lost.

choices.text: Use RDS as the source of truth, with ElastiCache in a cache-aside design and a TTL of no more than 30 seconds; fall back to RDS on a cache miss or failure
choices.explanation: This reduces database read load without losing updates committed to RDS if the cache is lost. Separately, use controls such as concurrency limits to prevent database overload during an outage.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Commit updates to the database, and use the cache to absorb read load.
learning.concept: With cache-aside, a cache miss triggers a database read and the result is placed in the cache. Manage freshness with a short TTL or invalidation on updates, and separately prepare for database load spikes during an outage.

check.prompt: What is the risk of keeping the latest value only in the cache and writing it to the database later?
check.answer: A failure before write-back could lose an update that was presented as committed.

title: Isolating Kinesis Reads
prompt: Five consumers share the same Kinesis Data Streams shard. When a backfill starts, reads for real-time detection fall behind. The writer has sufficient capacity. How can you isolate read capacity for detection without changing other applications’ checkpoints or the producer’s shard allocation?

choices.text: Register the detection consumer for Enhanced Fan-Out
choices.explanation: A registered consumer gets dedicated read throughput per shard.

choices.text: Increase the GetRecords retrieval limit for every standard consumer
choices.explanation: This does not isolate the shard’s read bandwidth shared by standard consumers.

choices.text: Keep standard reads and extend the shard’s retention period
choices.explanation: This increases the time available for replay, but contention from simultaneous reads with the backfill remains.

choices.text: Have the producer write the same event five times
choices.explanation: This increases write load, but consumers still share the read capacity of the same shard.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The contention is over the standard read capacity for the same shard, not write capacity.
learning.concept: A consumer registered for Enhanced Fan-Out gets dedicated read throughput for each shard. Changing the data retention period does not increase read capacity.

check.prompt: If you extend the retention period for the backfill, will detection get independent bandwidth?
check.answer: No. Retention determines how long data can be reread; Enhanced Fan-Out separates read capacity.

title: Reducing Lambda Startup Latency
prompt: A public API backed by Java Lambda experiences high load only for 30 minutes starting at 9 a.m. on weekdays. You want 200 initialized execution environments available for that period, without changing the existing alias. What should you configure? You do not want to pay for pre-provisioned capacity outside that period.

choices.text: Schedule Provisioned Concurrency for the alias to start shortly before the peak
choices.explanation: This can have the specified number of initialized environments ready by the scheduled time.

choices.text: Set Reserved Concurrency only
choices.explanation: This reserves or limits the concurrency allocation but does not ensure execution environments are initialized.

choices.text: Set API Gateway throttling to 200 requests per second
choices.explanation: This controls the request rate at the entry point; it does not pre-provision Lambda execution environments.

choices.text: Apply Lambda SnapStart to a published version
choices.explanation: SnapStart can speed up startup through restore, but it does not reserve 200 initialized concurrent execution environments for a specified time period.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The requirement is not just to reserve concurrency, but to have initialized environments ready at the start of the peak.
learning.concept: Reserved Concurrency reserves or limits concurrency. Provisioned Concurrency provides initialized environments for a specific version or alias and incurs charges while provisioned, even when unused.

check.prompt: Does setting Reserved Concurrency to 200 eliminate cold starts?
check.answer: No. It reserves concurrency but does not guarantee that environments are initialized.

title: Scaling Capacity Ahead of Traffic
prompt: An event site is about to open to the public, and its first sale starts at exactly 12:00 tomorrow. The required number of EC2 instances has been established through load testing, but the Auto Scaling group has no time-series production history. New instances take 8 minutes to prepare, and all instances must be running before the sale starts. Keep the change minimal. What should you do?

choices.text: Use only recent metric history and predictive scaling to estimate the first sales peak
choices.explanation: A one-time demand increase that has not been observed cannot necessarily be predicted from history.

choices.text: Use ordinary dynamic scaling after CPU exceeds a threshold at noon
choices.explanation: Capacity will increase only after waiting for the instances to launch.

choices.text: Set only the instance warmup to 8 minutes
choices.explanation: This adjusts how metrics are evaluated just after new instances launch; it does not launch them in advance.

choices.text: Set a scheduled action to increase capacity to the required number at a specified time well before the sale starts
choices.explanation: This directly uses the known start time and required capacity, allowing instances to finish initializing before the sale.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The start time and required capacity are known, and scaling after demand rises would be 8 minutes too late. Launch instances before demand increases.
learning.concept: A scheduled action changes capacity at a specified time. Warmup governs how metrics from new instances are treated; it does not start them early.

check.prompt: What if the start time is unknown, but long-term periodic demand has been observed?
check.answer: Predictive scaling may be appropriate if there is enough data. Scheduling is suited to a known one-time event.

title: Reducing Read Volume for Analytics Queries
prompt: You repeatedly aggregate only three columns for a specified date from several years of S3 logs using Athena. You can change the file format and layout during data preparation. You want to read as few files from other dates and as few unneeded columns from the specified date as possible. Which changes are required? Select two.

choices.text: Keep the file format and layout unchanged and enable Athena query result reuse
choices.explanation: Matching previous results can be reused, but this does not reduce the scan for the first run with a new date or new conditions.

choices.text: Combine the data into compressed JSON files by date, but do not register date partitions in the Glue table
choices.explanation: The files may be smaller, but this does not ensure file pruning by date or column-level scan reduction.

choices.text: Convert the logs to Parquet
choices.explanation: A columnar format lets Athena primarily scan the required columns.

choices.text: Partition the logs by date and filter on the date key in the query
choices.explanation: This lets Athena scan only the partition for the specified date.

choices.text: Keep the logs as one JSON object per file and specify the date in a WHERE clause
choices.explanation: Without date partitions, a WHERE clause alone cannot avoid reading out-of-range files.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Exclude files by date, then read only the required columns from the remaining files.
learning.concept: In Athena, including a date partition in the query condition narrows the data scanned. Parquet’s columnar format reduces reads of unneeded columns.

check.prompt: Does simply compressing JSON with gzip let Athena physically read only the required columns?
check.answer: No. Compression reduces stored size; columnar formats enable column pruning.

title: Global TCP Entry Point
prompt: A manufacturer's devices use a proprietary TCP protocol to connect to NLBs in two Regions. The devices can be provisioned with only a small number of fixed IPv4 addresses, and their firmware configuration cannot be updated during a failure. How should you provide Region selection and failover during network failures without waiting for clients' DNS caches to expire?

choices.text: Expose the NLBs using only low-TTL Route 53 records
choices.explanation: This depends on client-side DNS caching and does not provide a shared fixed entry-point IP.

choices.text: Configure the NLBs in both Regions as endpoints in Global Accelerator
choices.explanation: Global Accelerator accepts connections on fixed Anycast IP addresses and can route TCP traffic to healthy endpoints.

choices.text: Use a CloudFront origin group
choices.explanation: CloudFront is not intended to transparently forward arbitrary proprietary TCP traffic.

choices.text: Assign fixed EIPs to the NLB in each Region and return both through weighted DNS responses
choices.explanation: This provides a fixed IP in each Region, but which IP a client connects to still depends on the client resolving DNS again.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Provide clients with a fixed entry point and avoid relying on client-side DNS to make the decision between Regions.
learning.concept: Global Accelerator accepts traffic on fixed Anycast IP addresses and forwards TCP traffic to healthy regional endpoints, such as NLBs. It does not guarantee seamless transfer of existing connections during a failure.

check.prompt: Would lowering the Route 53 TTL provide an equivalent fixed entry point?
check.answer: No. It still depends on clients resolving DNS again and does not provide a shared fixed Anycast entry point.

title: SMB Compatibility
prompt: A Windows business application uses a share through a UNC path. You want to retain AD groups and existing Windows ACLs without changing the application, and automate share recovery after an AZ failure. The team cannot operate its own file-server cluster. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Use an FSx for Windows File Server Single-AZ deployment and restore backups in another AZ
choices.explanation: SMB compatibility is retained, but switching over requires a manual restore from backup.

choices.text: Expose SMB from a single Windows EC2 instance and replicate only EBS snapshots
choices.explanation: There is no managed Multi-AZ failover during a failure.

choices.text: Join an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ deployment to AD
choices.explanation: This supports SMB and Windows ACLs while maintaining service across AZs.

choices.text: Use Amazon EFS Regional directly as an SMB share for Windows clients
choices.explanation: EFS provides an NFS service and does not meet the existing SMB and Windows ACL requirements.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: This preserves SMB and AD compatibility while avoiding a manual restore after an AZ failure.
learning.concept: FSx for Windows File Server supports Windows ACLs. In a Multi-AZ deployment, it fails over to a standby file server in another AZ.

check.prompt: Would a backup from a Single-AZ deployment provide the same thing?
check.answer: It can be used to restore data, but unlike automatic failover, it requires restoring to a new environment.

title: Temporary HPC Scratch Space
prompt: Hundreds of Linux nodes must use input data from S3 as shared POSIX files for analysis with high parallel I/O. The results are written back to S3. You want managed integration for transfers to and from the bucket's input and output data, without synchronization tasks on individual nodes or custom synchronization scripts. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Copy input data from S3 to each compute node's EBS volume, then synchronize the results from each node after processing
choices.explanation: This allows parallel processing, but there is no shared POSIX namespace, and synchronization on each node is required.

choices.text: Mount EFS Regional and use the AWS CLI on each node to synchronize in both directions with S3
choices.explanation: This provides shared POSIX storage, but does not provide both Lustre for high parallel I/O and native integration with an S3 data repository.

choices.text: Attach a single EC2 instance's EBS volume as a local device to all nodes
choices.explanation: This does not provide an HPC shared file system across many nodes.

choices.text: Associate FSx for Lustre with an S3 data repository
choices.explanation: This provides an HPC parallel file system with integration to the data repository.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Use fast shared POSIX files during computation and rely on managed features for S3 integration of inputs and outputs.
learning.concept: FSx for Lustre is designed for parallel I/O. Associating an S3 data repository lets you manage imports and exports between S3 objects and the file system.

check.prompt: Would copying from S3 separately on each node provide the same configuration?
check.answer: No. There would be no shared namespace, and you would have to manage synchronization for each node.

title: DynamoDB Query Patterns
prompt: Orders are stored in DynamoDB with orderId as the primary key. The shipping team frequently retrieves orders whose warehouseId matches a value and whose ship-by date falls within a specified range. You must preserve the existing table and write key, and eventual consistency for index results is acceptable. How should you add this access pattern while minimizing the amount of data read?

choices.text: Create a GSI with the warehouse ID as the partition key and the ship-by date as the sort key, then use Query
choices.explanation: This directly retrieves the required range for a warehouse.

choices.text: Add an LSI to the existing table with orderId as the partition key
choices.explanation: You cannot add an LSI to an existing table, and even if one existed, you could not use Query based only on warehouseId.

choices.text: Use Scan with a warehouse ID and date FilterExpression
choices.explanation: Filtering happens after the items are read, so the scan itself cannot be avoided.

choices.text: Add a GSI keyed only on warehouseId and filter by ship-by date
choices.explanation: You can use Query for a warehouse, but reads cannot be limited by a date range, so extra items for that warehouse are also read.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Make both the warehouse match and date range key conditions instead of filtering after the read.
learning.concept: A GSI can use a partition key different from the base table's. Use Query with warehouseId and the date range. A filter is applied after reading.

check.prompt: What happens if you add a date filter to a GSI keyed only on warehouseId?
check.answer: You avoid Scan, but items for that warehouse outside the date range are also read before being filtered out.

title: CloudFront cache efficiency
prompt: Images are served through CloudFront. The origin uses the version query parameter to select an image version, while utm does not affect the image content. The analytics team only needs to be able to retrieve utm from CloudFront logs. Which configuration returns the correct response for each version while improving the cache hit rate when only utm differs for the same version?

choices.text: Disable caching for all requests
choices.explanation: This can retrieve the correct version, but it does not meet the requirement to improve the cache hit rate.

choices.text: Include all query parameters in the cache key
choices.explanation: Differences in utm would create separate cache entries for the same image.

choices.text: Apply a cache policy that includes only version in the cache key
choices.explanation: This separates cache entries only by the parameter that changes the content, so requests with different utm values can use the same cached response.

choices.text: Forward version to the origin but exclude it from the cache key, and set a positive TTL
choices.explanation: A cache miss can retrieve the correct version, but requests for different versions could hit the same cache entry.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Separate cache entries by version, which changes the response, and avoid creating more entries for utm, which is used for measurement only.
learning.concept: The values included in a cache key and those forwarded to the origin can be configured separately. Query parameters included in the cache key are also forwarded to the origin.

check.prompt: What happens if version is forwarded to the origin but is not included in the cache key?
check.answer: Even if the response is correct on a cache miss, a cached response for a different version could be returned.

title: Unpredictable access to S3 data
prompt: A video editing company stores assets of 4 MiB or larger for several years. When a project resumes, old assets may suddenly be read frequently, so access frequency cannot be predicted based on a fixed number of days since creation. Which configuration allows all assets to be retrieved in milliseconds, automatically tiers them based on access patterns, and avoids variable retrieval charges?

choices.text: Enable both Archive Access and Deep Archive Access in S3 Intelligent-Tiering
choices.explanation: Access patterns are tracked automatically, but objects in the optional archive tiers require asynchronous restoration.

choices.text: Transition objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 30 days
choices.explanation: Objects can be retrieved in milliseconds, but the transition follows a fixed rule, and retrieval charges apply if access increases again.

choices.text: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering without enabling the optional asynchronous archive tiers
choices.explanation: Objects are tiered based on observed access, maintaining millisecond access without retrieval charges.

choices.text: Transition objects to Standard-IA after 30 days and retrieve them as usual
choices.explanation: Retrieval charges may apply as access patterns change.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Old assets may be read frequently again, and they must remain immediately accessible. Do not assume low access based only on elapsed time.
learning.concept: S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers based on observed access. Monitoring and automation charges apply. Objects moved to the optional asynchronous archive tiers must be restored before they can be accessed.

check.prompt: Can Deep Archive Access be enabled while preserving immediate retrieval?
check.answer: No. Objects moved to that tier require restoration, so it should not be enabled for this requirement.

title: EC2 and Fargate usage charges
prompt: A service runs continuously on AWS, and you want to reduce its costs over one year. Some compute workloads may move from EC2 to Fargate during the year, and the remaining EC2 instances may change instance family or Region. How can a single commitment cover the lowest predictable usage amount?

choices.text: Create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation for the minimum capacity
choices.explanation: It reserves capacity but does not provide a long-term discount by itself.

choices.text: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the current instance family
choices.explanation: They do not cover changes beyond that family's scope or Fargate usage.

choices.text: Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for the current EC2 family and exchange them during migration
choices.explanation: The EC2 applicability can be changed, but the discount cannot be carried over to Fargate.

choices.text: Purchase Compute Savings Plans for an amount equal to the minimum usage
choices.explanation: They can cover eligible EC2 usage despite changes to the EC2 configuration and also apply to Fargate.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The compute platform may change from EC2 to Fargate, in addition to changes to the EC2 configuration. Check the scope of the discount.
learning.concept: Compute Savings Plans commit to an hourly spend amount and can apply to eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage. EC2 Instance Savings Plans have a narrower scope.

check.prompt: Why commit to the stable minimum usage amount rather than peak usage?
check.answer: You pay for unused commitment. Committing to variable usage can leave a surplus when usage falls below expectations.

title: Run batch jobs safely on Spot
prompt: A nightly AWS Batch job can resume on another instance from a checkpoint stored in S3 if a Spot interruption occurs. There is ample time before the deadline, and you want to benefit from spare capacity while spreading capacity options across both instance types and Availability Zones. Which configuration is required? Select two.

choices.text: Use the SPOT_PRICE_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED Spot allocation strategy and resume from the persistent checkpoint after an interruption
choices.explanation: This reduces interruption risk while allowing the job to resume on a different instance.

choices.text: Configure multiple families and Availability Zones as Spot capacity options
choices.explanation: This increases the number of available Spot pools and reduces dependence on any one pool being available.

choices.text: Include many Spot instance types but limit them all to the same Availability Zone
choices.explanation: This diversifies instance types but cannot take advantage of spare capacity differences across Availability Zones.

choices.text: Use only the cheapest Spot pool and write checkpoints to S3
choices.explanation: The job can resume after an interruption, but no capacity is available if the specified pool cannot launch instances.

choices.text: Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans and apply them to Spot charges
choices.explanation: Savings Plans do not apply to Spot usage charges.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Use lower-cost capacity while avoiding concentration in a particular Availability Zone or instance type.
learning.concept: A Spot pool is a combination of an instance type and an Availability Zone. Consider both price and capacity when choosing an allocation strategy, and provide alternative pools. Checkpoints help resume work after an interruption.

check.prompt: Can a persistent checkpoint prevent a Spot interruption itself?
check.answer: No. It helps limit lost work and resume after an interruption using other available capacity.

title: Unnecessary NAT data processing
prompt: EC2 instances in a private subnet send 3 TB to S3 in the same Region every day and also use the same NAT gateway for a small amount of external API traffic. Clients outside the VPC are out of scope. Which configuration avoids NAT processing charges and new endpoint processing charges for S3 transfers while keeping the external API route in place?

choices.text: Use a CloudFront distribution as the upload destination
choices.explanation: This does not avoid routing traffic from private EC2 instances to a public edge through the NAT gateway.

choices.text: Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the EC2 route table
choices.explanation: This routes only traffic destined for the S3 prefix away from the NAT gateway, while external API traffic can continue to use the NAT gateway.

choices.text: Send all traffic through an S3 interface endpoint
choices.explanation: This avoids the NAT gateway, but the endpoint has hourly and data processing charges. For traffic from the same VPC, the gateway endpoint has no endpoint charges and costs less.

choices.text: Add a route for the S3 destination prefix to a NAT gateway in the same AZ
choices.explanation: This may avoid cross-AZ transfer charges, but NAT data processing charges for S3 traffic remain.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Keep the NAT route required for the external API, and send only the high-volume S3 transfers through a different route.
learning.concept: For S3 in the same Region, add a route for the S3 destination prefix to an S3 gateway endpoint. Gateway endpoints have no hourly or data processing charges.

check.prompt: Can the NAT gateway be deleted after changing the S3 route?
check.answer: No. The external API still uses the NAT gateway under these conditions.

title: Separating EBS capacity from performance
prompt: A database on EC2 uses a 2 TiB gp2 volume. It has 800 GiB of data, and the volume was sized at 2 TiB to provide a 6,000 IOPS baseline. A 1 TiB volume has enough capacity, and the migration can take place during planned downtime. Which procedure reduces overprovisioned capacity while maintaining 6,000 IOPS?

choices.text: Reduce only the size of the existing gp2 volume to 1 TiB with ModifyVolume
choices.explanation: You cannot shrink an existing EBS volume with that operation, and gp2 baseline IOPS depend on volume size.

choices.text: Restore the existing snapshot directly to a 1 TiB gp3 volume
choices.explanation: A snapshot cannot be restored directly to a volume smaller than the original volume.

choices.text: Create a smaller gp3 volume with the required IOPS and throughput, migrate the data, and switch over
choices.explanation: With gp3, you can configure performance independently of capacity.

choices.text: Modify the existing 2 TiB volume in place to gp3 and specify 6,000 IOPS
choices.explanation: This separates performance settings from capacity, but the EBS volume remains 2 TiB, so the excess capacity is not reduced.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Separate the required IOPS from the required capacity, then move the data to a new volume that is actually smaller.
learning.concept: With gp3, performance can be configured independently of capacity. You cannot shrink an existing EBS volume, and a snapshot cannot be restored directly to a volume smaller than the original.

check.prompt: Can changing gp2 to gp3 in place halve the capacity charges?
check.answer: No. The capacity remains the same. You must migrate the data to a new, smaller volume.

title: Long-term log storage costs
prompt: Audit logs must be retained for 7 years. Immediate access is required for the first 30 days. After that, the logs are retrieved about once a year and must be restored within 48 hours. Objects are several MiB or larger, and new logs are added daily. Which lifecycle policy minimizes long-term storage costs as access frequency changes?

choices.text: Transition from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days
choices.explanation: This preserves immediate access for the initial period and then moves the data to a low-cost tier that supports bulk retrieval, typically within 48 hours.

choices.text: Transition from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days
choices.explanation: This meets the retrieval requirement, but for a 7-year retention period with a 48-hour window, Deep Archive has a lower storage rate.

choices.text: Keep the objects in S3 Standard for the entire period
choices.explanation: This costs more than necessary for long-term, infrequent access.

choices.text: Transition to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days and keep the objects there
choices.explanation: Millisecond access is not required, and the long retention period makes a lower-cost archive class suitable.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · アーカイブの取り出し方式

learning.reason: Immediate access is needed for the first 30 days; afterward, retrieval can wait for restoration. Use a low-cost tier for most of the retention period.
learning.concept: S3 Glacier Deep Archive objects must be restored before a normal GET. Retrieval times vary by method; Bulk retrieval typically takes up to 48 hours.

check.prompt: What if the logs must remain immediately accessible after the first 30 days?
check.answer: Deep Archive would not be suitable. Compare the storage and retrieval charges for classes that provide immediate access.

sourceLabel: AWS Official material · Archive retrieval options

title: Irregular DynamoDB workload
prompt: A new service uses DynamoDB and has bursts lasting a few seconds on some days, but is idle most of the time. The timing of requests cannot be predicted, and the spikes are within the known scaling range for on-demand mode. Which setting avoids provisioning peak capacity in advance while limiting initial throttling and idle costs?

choices.text: Always configure provisioned capacity at the expected peak
choices.explanation: You would pay for provisioned capacity during idle periods as well.

choices.text: Schedule increases to provisioned capacity only during previously observed busy hours
choices.explanation: Because the burst timing cannot be predicted, this cannot precede every burst.

choices.text: Configure low provisioned capacity and use DynamoDB Auto Scaling to increase it based on utilization
choices.explanation: This can respond to sustained load, but a short spike may end before it is detected and capacity is adjusted.

choices.text: Use on-demand capacity mode
choices.explanation: You pay per request, and the mode can respond to variable demand without allocating capacity in advance.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The short bursts cannot be predicted, and keeping peak capacity provisioned would waste capacity for most of the time.
learning.concept: DynamoDB on-demand mode charges based on request volume. Sudden increases well beyond previous peaks or outside quotas and other scaling limits can still cause throttling.

check.prompt: Does switching to on-demand mean every increase in demand can be handled without limits?
check.answer: No. Check previous peaks, quotas, key distribution, and other scaling limits.

title: Log Queries and Retention
prompt: Service logs are sent to CloudWatch Logs, where they are currently retained indefinitely. Select the two changes needed to search logs from the most recent 14 days immediately with Logs Insights, retain older logs for 365 days to meet regulatory requirements, and reduce long-term storage costs without changing the log producer. Preserve existing logs. Select two.

choices.text: Replace immediate 14-day search in CloudWatch Logs with Glacier restoration alone.
choices.explanation: Restoration is required, so this does not meet the requirement for immediate, routine searches.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch Logs subscription to continuously deliver new logs through Firehose to S3, and configure a 365-day retention lifecycle in S3.
choices.explanation: This moves long-term storage to S3 without changing the existing log collection side. A subscription alone does not move existing logs.

choices.text: Export existing logs to S3 once, then set the CloudWatch Logs retention period to 14 days.
choices.explanation: This moves the logs already stored, but new logs will not be retained long term after they exceed 14 days.

choices.text: Backfill the existing logs for the required period to S3, verify continuity with the new delivery stream, and then set CloudWatch Logs retention to 14 days.
choices.explanation: Preserving existing logs before changing the retention period avoids gaps in the audit period while reducing storage costs in the search store.

choices.text: Set only the CloudWatch Logs retention period to 14 days.
choices.explanation: Without a separate archive, this would lose historical data required by regulation.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · 既存ログのエクスポート

learning.reason: Separate the store used for recent searches from the long-term storage destination. Shortening retention before accounting for existing logs creates gaps.
learning.concept: Use a subscription to continuously deliver new logs, and use an S3 export to migrate existing logs. Verify continuity and check for gaps or duplicates during the transition before changing the retention setting.

check.prompt: If I create a subscription now, will it also move logs from six months ago?
check.answer: No. Plan a separate retrospective transfer.

sourceLabel: AWS official documentation · Exporting existing logs

title: Incomplete S3 Uploads
prompt: More clients are starting uploads and leaving without calling the completion API. S3 storage costs have risen even though the number of completed objects has stayed the same. Normal multipart uploads complete within 24 hours, and completed objects follow the existing retention rules. What should you do to reduce costs with the least operational overhead?

choices.text: Apply a two-day expiration rule to noncurrent versions.
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts are not managed as noncurrent object versions.

choices.text: Use a lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads that are more than two days old.
choices.explanation: This deletes parts from old incomplete uploads while allowing time for normal uploads to complete.

choices.text: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to move incomplete parts between tiers.
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts cannot be deleted by moving objects between storage tiers.

choices.text: Expire current objects after two days.
choices.explanation: This setting applies to completed objects. Use the dedicated lifecycle rule to remove incomplete parts.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: The increased charges may be caused by parts from uploads that have neither completed nor been aborted, rather than by completed objects.
learning.concept: The lifecycle action AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload stops incomplete uploads after the specified number of days from initiation. It is separate from expiration of completed objects.

check.prompt: If a normal upload takes three days, is it appropriate to abort it after two days?
check.answer: That could abort a normal upload. Set the period longer than the time needed for normal processing.

title: Idle Costs for an Analytics Environment
prompt: Each department aggregates Parquet data in S3 using standard SQL only a few times a week. Avoid loading the data into a dedicated warehouse, and set a per-query limit on the number of bytes scanned. Which option requires the fewest configuration steps and does not keep a server running while idle?

choices.text: Use Athena on-demand queries, with a workgroup and scan limit configured for each department.
choices.explanation: This does not require a server to remain provisioned and lets you control the amount scanned by each query.

choices.text: Run Presto continuously on EC2 and share it across departments.
choices.explanation: EC2 costs accrue during idle periods, even for intermittent workloads.

choices.text: Use Redshift Serverless to query external data and set an RPU usage limit for each workgroup.
choices.explanation: This provides serverless analytics, but an RPU usage limit is not a per-query limit on bytes scanned.

choices.text: Embed standard SQL in AWS Glue Spark jobs and use a shared execution allocation across departments.
choices.explanation: This can avoid idle-time charges, but it requires additional implementation to meet the scan-limit requirement that Athena supports.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · Athenaのクエリ別データ使用量制御

learning.reason: Avoid a continuously running server while limiting the amount read by each query.
learning.concept: Athena reads data in S3 directly using SQL. For on-demand queries, the amount scanned is a cost driver, and a workgroup per-query limit can cancel queries that exceed it.

check.prompt: Can a workgroup per-query limit be treated as a monthly budget cap for a department?
check.answer: No. A per-query limit is separate from monitoring cumulative monthly spend or usage.

sourceLabel: AWS official documentation · Per-query data usage controls in Athena

title: Image Version Management
prompt: Each ECR image has exactly one tag, beginning with either ci- or release-. Keep every release image for 90 days after it is pushed, and keep the 10 newest CI images regardless of age. How can you manage this without creating an external cleanup job?

choices.text: Create tag-specific rules that expire CI images after 10 days and release images after 90 days.
choices.explanation: If many CI images are created in one day, this keeps more than 10 days' worth; age alone does not enforce a count limit.

choices.text: Delete images across the repository when the total exceeds 10.
choices.explanation: This could unintentionally violate the 90-day retention requirement for production releases.

choices.text: Use separate rules for each tag prefix: expire CI images exceeding the 10-image count, and expire release images more than 90 days after being pushed.
choices.explanation: Separate tag-based rules can represent the different count-based and age-based retention criteria.

choices.text: Automatically delete old images during ECR scans.
choices.explanation: Image scanning detects vulnerabilities; it does not manage retained image versions.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · ECRライフサイクルポリシー

learning.reason: Manage CI images by the number of newest images to retain and release images by age since push, with each rule scoped to the appropriate tags.
learning.concept: ECR lifecycle policies can combine tag criteria with count-based or age-based rules. Since the rules apply to images, review the evaluation result if an image has multiple tags.

check.prompt: What if the same image starts receiving both CI and release tags?
check.answer: That breaks the current assumption. Recheck rule priority and preview results to ensure release images are not selected for expiration.

sourceLabel: AWS official documentation · ECR lifecycle policies

title: Scheduled Long-Running Container Jobs
prompt: A few times each month, a task definition that has been validated on ECS runs a two-hour aggregation job. It must start at a fixed time, use no compute resources on days when there is no work, and require no management of EC2 hosts. Interruption due to Spot capacity reclamation during processing is unacceptable. Which design requires the fewest changes?

choices.text: Schedule Fargate Spot tasks
choices.explanation: A task may be terminated partway through when capacity is reclaimed.

choices.text: Run the container as a single two-hour Lambda invocation
choices.explanation: A single Lambda invocation can run for at most 15 minutes.

choices.text: Have EventBridge Scheduler call ECS RunTask and use regular Fargate capacity
choices.explanation: The task runs only when started, users do not manage hosts, and Spot reclamation is not part of this option.

choices.text: Keep an ECS service on Fargate running with at least one task, and use cron inside the task to start the aggregation
choices.explanation: Host management is unnecessary, but the task is billed even when no aggregation is running.

source.label: AWS公式試験ガイド（出題範囲）

learning.reason: Start the long-running container as a scheduled one-off task, avoiding idle capacity overnight and Spot reclamation.
learning.concept: EventBridge Scheduler calls ECS RunTask at the scheduled time. Regular Fargate capacity requires no underlying EC2 hosts and avoids the minimum task count of an always-on service.

check.prompt: Are successful task launch and successful task completion the same thing?
check.answer: No. A job can fail even after RunTask is accepted, so observe the task's terminal status.

title: Reducing NAT Costs for Service Connectivity
prompt: Twelve VPCs contain order-processing workers. They currently access DynamoDB in the same Region only, using a NAT gateway in a shared VPC through Transit Gateway. They have no other internet use. In preparation for increased data transfer, how can you eliminate both the NAT processing charge and the TGW data processing charge for this traffic?

choices.text: Move a NAT gateway into each worker VPC and remove the routes to the shared VPC
choices.explanation: This removes Transit Gateway from the path, but NAT processing charges remain.

choices.text: Move the shared VPC's NAT gateway to an Availability Zone geographically closer to each worker
choices.explanation: This does not reduce the amount of traffic that goes through Transit Gateway and NAT.

choices.text: Create one DynamoDB gateway endpoint in the shared VPC and let all workers share it over Transit Gateway
choices.explanation: A gateway endpoint cannot be used transitively through Transit Gateway.

choices.text: Create a DynamoDB gateway endpoint in each worker VPC and associate it with the route tables
choices.explanation: This routes traffic directly to DynamoDB from within each VPC, removing NAT and Transit Gateway from this path.

source.label: AWS公式資料 · DynamoDBゲートウェイエンドポイント

learning.reason: To remove both NAT and Transit Gateway from the traffic path, connect directly to DynamoDB from each worker VPC.
learning.concept: A DynamoDB gateway endpoint is associated with route tables in a VPC. A gateway endpoint in a shared VPC cannot be used transitively across Transit Gateway.

check.prompt: What if you only move a NAT gateway into each worker VPC?
check.answer: You may avoid Transit Gateway charges, but NAT data processing charges for DynamoDB traffic remain.

sourceLabel: AWS Official Materials · DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints

title: Choose Lambda Memory Using Measured Runtime
prompt: Compare memory settings for an on-demand Lambda Event Function running in the same Region and with the same instruction set. Using the same representative input, measure the average billed duration per invocation and the 95th-percentile response time. Invocation counts and request charges are identical, and no additional storage is used. Which option minimizes execution-time charges while keeping the 95th-percentile response time at or below 450 milliseconds?

choices.text: 512 MB. Average billed duration: 800 milliseconds; 95th-percentile response time: 900 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: This is about 0.40 GB-seconds. Its response time exceeds 450 milliseconds.

choices.text: 1,024 MB. Average billed duration: 350 milliseconds; 95th-percentile response time: 430 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: This is 0.35 GB-seconds. It has the lowest execution-time charge among the options that meet the response-time requirement.

choices.text: 1,536 MB. Average billed duration: 280 milliseconds; 95th-percentile response time: 310 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: This is 0.42 GB-seconds. It meets the response-time requirement, but costs more than the 1,024 MB option.

choices.text: 2,048 MB. Average billed duration: 220 milliseconds; 95th-percentile response time: 260 milliseconds.
choices.explanation: This is 0.44 GB-seconds. It is the fastest option, but has the largest memory setting.

source.label: AWS Lambda — リクエストとGB秒に基づく料金

learning.reason: The 1,024 MB option uses 0.35 GB-seconds, less than the 0.42 GB-seconds at 1,536 MB and 0.44 GB-seconds at 2,048 MB, while meeting the response-time requirement.
learning.concept: Lambda Event Function execution-time charges are based on allocated memory multiplied by billed duration. Reducing memory also reduces CPU and can increase runtime.

sourceLabel: AWS Lambda — Pricing Based on Requests and GB-seconds

title: Lower EFS Costs Based on Access Frequency at the Same File Path
prompt: An editing team uses an existing EFS Regional file system over NFS. After a project ends, its files are read only once every few months and make up most of the stored data. If the project resumes, the team must be able to read them immediately at the same paths, and after the first access they must return to a frequently accessed tier without on-demand manual work. What should the team do?

choices.text: Configure migration to EFS IA and disable migration to Standard.
choices.explanation: The files remain readable at the same paths, but access after a project resumes does not automatically move them back to Standard.

choices.text: Export the files from EFS to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and delete the originals from EFS.
choices.explanation: This may reduce storage costs, but it requires retrieval from another service, so the files are not immediately readable at their existing NFS paths.

choices.text: Change only EFS throughput so that infrequently accessed files automatically move to a lower-cost tier.
choices.explanation: Changing the throughput mode does not configure lifecycle migration for individual files.

choices.text: Configure EFS lifecycle management to move files with no access to IA and return them to Standard on first access.
choices.explanation: The content remains available at the same paths, and files that become active again can return to Standard.

source.label: Amazon EFS — ライフサイクル管理

learning.reason: Move files to EFS IA after a period without access, then return them to Standard upon the first access to IA. The file paths do not change.
learning.concept: EFS lifecycle management can be applied to the file system. Configure tier transitions and transitions back based on usage.

title: Lowering storage costs for DynamoDB order history
prompt: After an order is finalized, its history is stored for several years in a separate DynamoDB table. Support staff who know the order ID look up a record a few times per month and need to retrieve it with GetItem in under one second. Storage dominates the bill, and an estimate shows that the storage savings exceed any increase in read and write costs. Which change meets these requirements without changing the data model or API?

choices.text: Change the history table’s table class to DynamoDB Standard-IA.
choices.explanation: This lowers the per-GB storage price while preserving the existing retrieval method in DynamoDB.

choices.text: Keep the history table in the Standard table class and switch only its read capacity to on-demand.
choices.explanation: Changing the capacity mode does not lower the storage price. DynamoDB capacity modes also do not switch only read capacity.

choices.text: Add a DynamoDB Accelerator cache and leave the history table unchanged.
choices.explanation: This can speed up frequent reads, but it does not reduce the existing storage costs and adds the cost of the cache.

choices.text: Move the history to S3 Glacier Deep Archive and continue retrieving it with the same DynamoDB GetItem call.
choices.explanation: GetItem cannot retrieve objects that have been moved out of DynamoDB. This option also does not meet the immediate-access requirement.

source.label: Amazon DynamoDB — テーブルクラス

learning.reason: When storage costs dominate and access is infrequent, DynamoDB Standard-IA is a good fit.
learning.concept: A table class changes storage and read/write prices. A capacity mode changes how read and write capacity is provisioned and billed.

title: Reducing operating hours for a weekday-only development database
prompt: A development team uses a single-AZ RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance during weekday business hours. It is not used on weekends, and the team wants to resume the same DB with the same endpoint and data before work starts on Monday. Which approach reduces DB instance-hour charges at night and on weekends while preserving the existing storage and backup configuration?

choices.text: Take a snapshot before the weekend, delete the DB, and restore it every Monday.
choices.explanation: This can stop compute charges, but a restore creates a new DB, which does not meet the requirement to resume the same DB.

choices.text: Close all database connections outside business hours and leave the DB instance running.
choices.explanation: Even with no connections, a running provisioned DB continues to incur DB instance-hour charges.

choices.text: Schedule the DB to stop after the workday and start it before work begins, allowing time for startup.
choices.explanation: This resumes the same DB instance, preserving its data and endpoint, and reduces instance-hour charges while it is stopped.

choices.text: Lower the maximum for storage autoscaling at night to reduce DB instance charges.
choices.explanation: Storage settings do not change how long the DB instance runs.

source.label: Amazon RDS — DBインスタンスの一時停止

learning.reason: Automating stop and start lets the same DB instance run only when needed. A weekend stop lasts fewer than seven days.
learning.concept: When an RDS DB instance is stopped, charges for provisioned storage and applicable backups remain. It starts automatically after being stopped for seven consecutive days.

sourceLabel: Amazon RDS — temporarily stopping a DB instance

title: Keeping EFS backups warm initially, then in cold storage
prompt: AWS Backup is used to retain EFS backups that support transition to cold storage. Keep each backup warm for the first 30 days after it is created, then move it to cold storage. The audit team specifies an expiration date 120 days after creation in the plan. How should the cold transition and expiration be configured?

choices.text: Transition the backup 90 days after creation and expire it 120 days after creation.
choices.explanation: This leaves only 30 days in cold storage, which is less than the required minimum of 90 days.

choices.text: Transition the backup 30 days after creation and expire it 120 days after creation.
choices.explanation: The backup remains warm for the first 30 days and stays in cold storage for the remaining 90 days.

choices.text: Transition the backup 30 days after creation and expire it 90 days after creation.
choices.explanation: The total retention period is 90 days, shorter than the audit requirement. The cold-storage period is also only 60 days.

choices.text: Transition the backup immediately after creation and expire it 120 days after creation.
choices.explanation: Meeting the cold-storage duration alone does not satisfy the requirement to keep the backup warm for the first 30 days.

source.label: AWS Backup — バックアッププランの保持設定

learning.reason: Transitioning after 30 days and expiring 120 days after creation provides 30 warm days followed by the minimum 90 days in cold storage.
learning.concept: When AWS Backup is configured to transition recovery points to cold storage, the retention period measured from creation must be at least 90 days longer than the transition date.

sourceLabel: AWS Backup — backup plan retention settings

title: Checking EC2 memory headroom beyond CPU metrics
prompt: CPU utilization is low on a Linux EC2 instance that runs image conversion. A test with a smaller instance caused memory exhaustion during daytime processing. Compute Optimizer is opted in, and only the standard EC2 metrics are currently available. Choose two actions that provide measured memory usage for each instance to inform rightsizing recommendations without adding an external monitoring service.

choices.text: Install the CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instance and publish mem_used_percent to the CWAgent namespace.
choices.explanation: This collects a Linux guest OS memory metric that Compute Optimizer analyzes.

choices.text: Only enable EC2 detailed monitoring so AWS/EC2 sends guest OS memory utilization.
choices.explanation: Detailed monitoring changes the frequency of default metrics; it does not collect guest OS memory utilization.

choices.text: Publish a host group’s aggregated average memory value with only the team name as a dimension.
choices.explanation: A group average cannot be mapped to the memory utilization of each individual EC2 instance.

choices.text: Include the InstanceId dimension in the published memory metric.
choices.explanation: Compute Optimizer needs InstanceId to associate the published metric with an individual EC2 instance.

choices.text: Log processing time in the application and specify the log group as Compute Optimizer’s EC2 memory input.
choices.explanation: Application processing time does not represent memory utilization, and specifying a log group alone does not provide the required metric.

source.label: AWS Compute Optimizer — EC2のメモリ使用率

learning.reason: Publish Linux mem_used_percent to CWAgent with the CloudWatch agent and use the InstanceId dimension so each measurement can be associated with an instance.
learning.concept: Low CPU utilization does not necessarily mean there is ample memory. Publish measured values in a format that Compute Optimizer recognizes.

sourceLabel: AWS Compute Optimizer — EC2 memory utilization

title: Reducing the cost of older versions for objects with different update rates
prompt: Delivery files are stored under assets/ in a versioned S3 bucket. Which configuration leaves the current version untouched, retains previous versions for at least 30 days after they become noncurrent and retains the three newest noncurrent versions? It must not delete up to three versions of keys that are updated infrequently, avoid manual listing, and delete only versions that exceed the retention requirements.

choices.text: Configure expiration of current versions under assets/ and delete versions 30 days after creation.
choices.explanation: Expiration of current versions applies to current versions and does not compare either the time since a version became noncurrent or the number of newer noncurrent versions.

choices.text: Expire noncurrent versions under assets/ after 30 days without specifying how many newer versions to retain.
choices.explanation: Expiration based only on age could delete all three versions of a key that is updated infrequently.

choices.text: Automatically archive the three newest previous versions under assets/ and configure 30-day expiration for current versions.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to keep current versions, and it does not control deletion of excess previous versions.

choices.text: Filter by the assets/ prefix and specify both 30 days since becoming noncurrent and retention of the three newest noncurrent versions in the same noncurrent-version expiration action.
choices.explanation: This expires only previous versions that meet both conditions and leaves current versions untouched.

source.label: Amazon S3 — ライフサイクルの非現行版の失効

learning.reason: Use a noncurrent-version expiration rule with an assets/ filter, and specify both the number of days since becoming noncurrent and the number of newer versions to retain.
learning.concept: A noncurrent-version expiration rule can combine an age threshold with a version-count threshold. Versions are deleted only after the specified newer versions have been retained and the age threshold has passed.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Expiring noncurrent versions in a lifecycle rule

title: Allocating research data storage and download charges to different organizations
prompt: A research institute shares large volumes of collected measurement data from a general purpose S3 bucket. Participating institutions in other AWS accounts download the data over the network using authenticated S3 API requests. The institute must continue paying storage charges, while each institution’s account is charged directly for successful download requests and data transfer. Which two measures meet these requirements while retaining the existing bucket and avoiding interorganization expense settlement?

choices.text: Have each institution assume a role in the research institute’s AWS account and use those credentials for Requester Pays retrievals.
choices.explanation: The account associated with the assumed role is charged. Using a role in the institute’s account would not charge each participating institution directly.

choices.text: Configure the source S3 bucket as a Requester Pays bucket.
choices.explanation: This enables S3 to charge the requester for applicable download costs.

choices.text: Create only an S3 access point for each institution and leave the payer settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: An access point is a unit for managing access; it does not change the default bucket cost allocation as required.

choices.text: Change the bucket’s resource tags for each participating institution and use cost allocation tags alone to transfer charges to each institution’s AWS bill.
choices.explanation: Cost allocation tags are labels for analyzing costs. They do not configure direct billing to another account.

choices.text: Have each institution use authorized credentials from its own account and include Requester Pays billing consent in its S3 download requests.
choices.explanation: This identifies the requester’s account for billing. The bucket owner continues to pay storage charges.

source.label: Amazon S3 — Requester Paysの課金

learning.reason: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket, then have each institution retrieve objects with permissions from its own account and the parameter that accepts the charges.
learning.concept: Requester Pays applies to authenticated requests. The requester pays the request and data transfer charges for successful GET requests, while the owner pays for storage.

title: Extending existing EC2 Reserved Instance discounts across sizes and Availability Zones
prompt: Linux/UNIX EC2 instances with default tenancy run continuously across multiple Availability Zones in the same Region. They are being moved gradually to different sizes in the same instance family. The procurement policy requires EC2 Reserved Instances, and there are enough normalized units across the fleet to cover all eligible sizes. Which purchase scope applies discounts after the size changes without reserving launch capacity in a particular Availability Zone?

choices.text: Purchase zonal Reserved Instances for the current size in the Availability Zone where the most instances run.
choices.explanation: These are limited to that Availability Zone and size, so the discount does not extend to a different size or another Availability Zone after the migration.

choices.text: Create only targeted On-Demand Capacity Reservations in each Availability Zone.
choices.explanation: These reserve capacity, but an On-Demand Capacity Reservation does not itself provide a Reserved Instance discount.

choices.text: Purchase Regional Reserved Instances in the same Region for the applicable instance family, operating system, and tenancy.
choices.explanation: The discount can apply across Availability Zones in the same Region and across sizes in the same family, according to normalized units.

choices.text: Purchase zonal Reserved Instances of the current size in each Availability Zone and assume they will automatically apply to size changes as long as the family stays the same.
choices.explanation: Purchasing in multiple Availability Zones does not give zonal reservations size flexibility. It also reserves capacity that the requirements do not call for.

source.label: Amazon EC2 — リージョンとAZのリザーブドインスタンス

learning.reason: A Regional Reserved Instance provides size and Availability Zone flexibility within the same instance family when the operating system and tenancy match the stated assumptions.
learning.concept: Discount eligibility and capacity reservation are separate properties. A zonal Reserved Instance reserves capacity of the specified size in the specified Availability Zone.

sourceLabel: Amazon EC2 — Regional and zonal Reserved Instances

title: Reducing edge delivery costs while maintaining global reach
prompt: Images are served through a pay-as-you-go CloudFront distribution. Most users are in North America and Europe. Users in other regions must still be able to retrieve images, although increased latency there is acceptable. Which method reduces the delivery rate by selecting the edge locations used, without changing the origin or authentication?

choices.text: Change the CloudFront price class to a narrower class that includes the primary regions, allowing delivery from more distant edge locations in regions outside that class.
choices.explanation: This setting narrows the range of delivery locations. It does not deny users by country, so delivery remains available outside the primary regions.

choices.text: Use CloudFront geographic restrictions to allow only countries in the primary regions, while keeping the price class set to all regions.
choices.explanation: This denies users who are not on the country allow list, contrary to the requirement that they can still retrieve the images.

choices.text: Keep the price class set to all regions and shorten CloudFront TTLs to reduce cache responses from higher-priced regions.
choices.explanation: TTL controls cache freshness; it does not select the edge locations whose delivery rates apply.

choices.text: Keep the price class unchanged and move the origin to a Region closer to the primary users to change the delivery billing regions.
choices.explanation: The origin’s location and the price class for edge delivery to viewers are separate settings.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — ディストリビューションの料金クラス

learning.reason: A lower price class that covers the primary regions narrows the set of higher-cost delivery locations while still allowing users in other regions to access the content.
learning.concept: Price classes are a choice of edge delivery price and performance. They serve a different purpose from allowing or denying access by country.

title: Lower ingestion costs for new audit logs without changing existing logs
prompt: Several TB of application logs are sent to a CloudWatch Logs Standard log group each month. During investigations, they are searched with CloudWatch Logs Insights QL. This search must remain available, but no Standard-only features such as metric filters, Live Tail, or subscriptions are used. Which design lowers the ingestion price for new logs while preserving the existing collected data and its retention period?

choices.text: Change the class of the current log group to Essentials and continue sending logs to the same destination.
choices.explanation: A log group's class cannot be changed after it is created.

choices.text: Switch new logs to the Delivery class for Lambda, retain them for the same period, and search them with Logs Insights QL.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch-side retention for Delivery is fixed at 2 days, and Logs Insights queries are not available.

choices.text: Keep using the current Standard class and shorten only the retention period.
choices.explanation: This affects storage costs but does not change the ingestion price, and it does not meet the requirement to preserve the retention period.

choices.text: Create a new log group in the Essentials class and send new logs to it. Keep the current group and its existing retention settings.
choices.explanation: This can lower the ingestion cost for new logs, which remain searchable with Logs Insights QL. Existing logs remain available in the original group for their original retention period.

source.label: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — ログクラスと機能

learning.reason: Create a new Essentials log group and switch the destination for new logs. Keep existing logs in the current group.
learning.concept: The log class is specified when a group is created. Essentials (formerly Infrequent Access) lowers ingestion costs while still supporting Logs Insights QL.

sourceLabel: Amazon CloudWatch Logs — Log classes and features

title: Keep infrequently accessed logs searchable in OpenSearch
prompt: Logs are accumulated daily in a managed OpenSearch Service domain. New indexes need to support writes and low-latency queries, but indexes older than 30 days are no longer changed and are queried only a few times per month. The older indexes must remain searchable from the same domain without reattaching and reingesting them, while reducing the capacity required on hot nodes. The domain supports UltraWarm. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Detach older indexes to OpenSearch cold storage and search them as usual while they remain detached.
choices.explanation: To search a cold index, it must first be reattached to the warm tier.

choices.text: Change the shard configuration of older indexes but keep them on the same hot tier.
choices.explanation: Even if shards are consolidated, hot-tier block capacity is still required to store the older data.

choices.text: Keep only snapshots of older indexes in S3, delete the indexes, and query the snapshots directly with the same search API.
choices.explanation: The usual search API cannot query a snapshot of a deleted index directly; the index must be restored.

choices.text: Move indexes to UltraWarm after their write period ends, and continue reading them from the same domain.
choices.explanation: This moves older indexes to a lower-cost, read-only tier where they can be searched without reingestion.

source.label: Amazon OpenSearch Service — UltraWarm

learning.reason: Moving immutable indexes to UltraWarm reduces the capacity needed on the hot tier while allowing queries to continue from the same domain.
learning.concept: UltraWarm is suitable for indexes that are no longer being written to. A cold-storage index must be reattached to the warm tier before it can be queried.

title: Reduce API Gateway costs while retaining required authorization
prompt: A single-page application calls a public HTTPS JSON API. API Gateway must provide path-based Lambda integrations, authorization with JWTs from an external IdP, and CORS. API keys, usage plans, and request-body validation are not needed, and the team does not want to add a custom Lambda for authorization. Which choice meets the requirements and lowers the per-request price?

choices.text: Create a Lambda authorizer for a REST API and parse the JWT inside the function.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirements, but adds a custom authorization function and incurs REST API pricing.

choices.text: Use an HTTP API and configure its native JWT authorizer with the external IdP's issuer and audience.
choices.explanation: This validates JWTs without custom authorization code while retaining CORS and Lambda integrations.

choices.text: Create an HTTP API and use API keys and usage plans in place of an authorizer.
choices.explanation: HTTP APIs do not provide usage plans. API keys also cannot validate JWTs from an external IdP.

choices.text: Replace the API Gateway endpoint with a WebSocket API and migrate all HTTP clients to persistent connections.
choices.explanation: This API is for persistent, bidirectional connections and does not meet the requirement to preserve the existing HTTPS request contract.

source.label: Amazon API Gateway — REST APIとHTTP API

learning.reason: The HTTP API's JWT authorizer, Lambda integrations, and CORS provide the required features at a lower per-request cost without requiring an additional authorization function.
learning.concept: HTTP APIs suit workloads that need a lighter feature set. Consider a REST API when usage plans or detailed request validation within API Gateway are required.

sourceLabel: Amazon API Gateway — REST APIs and HTTP APIs

title: Aggregate simultaneous cache misses across regions
prompt: Several-GB videos are delivered through CloudFront. Each video version has its own URL. When the same version is published in multiple regions at the same time, cache misses from each region cause a surge in reads of the same object from the S3 origin. Which measure aggregates origin fetches across regions while preserving the published URLs and TTL?

choices.text: Exclude all query strings from the cache policy key.
choices.explanation: Versions are distinguished by the URL path. Changing how query strings are handled cannot aggregate the first fetches for the same URL across multiple regions.

choices.text: Invalidate each version's object at publication time so every region retrieves the latest content.
choices.explanation: An invalidation removes cached content; it does not add a shared layer that aggregates cache misses.

choices.text: Enable Origin Shield in the Region closest to the origin.
choices.explanation: It handles cache misses from multiple regions at the same layer, reducing origin requests for the same object.

choices.text: Create another CloudFront distribution pointing to the same S3 origin and route users to a distribution by region.
choices.explanation: This adds independent delivery paths but does not aggregate misses from multiple regions in a shared cache in front of the origin.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront — Origin Shield

learning.reason: Aggregate requests from regional caches that use the same origin into the shared Origin Shield cache layer.
learning.concept: Origin Shield adds a layer to the existing cache hierarchy. It is not intended to change cache keys or consolidate version-specific URLs.

title: Increase read capacity while preserving existing Valkey key placement
prompt: An ElastiCache for Valkey cluster-mode-disabled configuration sends writes and reads to a single primary. Reads for a list API have increased, but write volume is unchanged, and eventual consistency is acceptable for the list. Which configuration distributes read load across multiple nodes while preserving the existing key placement?

choices.text: Add replicas, but continue sending all reads and writes to the primary endpoint.
choices.explanation: Adding replicas does not change where reads sent to the primary endpoint are served: they still reach the primary.

choices.text: Add replicas and use a connection pool that sends writes to the primary endpoint and reads to the reader endpoint.
choices.explanation: When the application uses separate connections for each purpose, reads can be distributed across multiple replicas without changing the write destination.

choices.text: Enable cluster mode, redistribute keys across multiple shards, and distribute writes across the shards.
choices.explanation: This can scale the workload, but redistributing keys does not meet the requirement to preserve the existing key placement.

choices.text: After each failover, obtain the new primary's node endpoint and direct all reads to it.
choices.explanation: Reads would still concentrate on a single node after a failover, so this would not distribute the load.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCache — 接続エンドポイント

learning.reason: Add read replicas, send read connections to the reader endpoint, and send writes to the primary endpoint.
learning.concept: The reader endpoint returns replica endpoints in rotation through DNS. Use multiple connections to distribute load; it does not route individual requests within a single connection.

title: Reduce empty SQS receives with workers that can wait for messages
prompt: A standard SQS queue receives a notification only once every few minutes, even during the day. Always-on workers call ReceiveMessage at short intervals, and most responses are empty. When a new message enters the queue, the workers should receive it without waiting for the next fixed interval. If the existing queue must continue to be used, what should be changed?

choices.text: Increase the visibility timeout to 20 seconds and keep short-interval polling.
choices.explanation: This adjusts how long a message being processed is hidden before it can be delivered again; it does not make ReceiveMessage wait when no message is available.

choices.text: Change MaxNumberOfMessages from 1 to 10 and leave the wait time at 0 seconds.
choices.explanation: This raises the maximum number of messages received, but an empty queue still returns an empty response without waiting.

choices.text: Change the workers' short polling to an interval of one minute.
choices.explanation: This can reduce empty requests, but a new message may have to wait for the next scheduled call.

choices.text: Set a maximum wait time of 20 seconds for ReceiveMessage and set the workers' HTTP response timeout to a value longer than that.
choices.explanation: This enables long polling, so a worker can receive a message as soon as it appears.

source.label: Amazon SQS — ショートポーリングとロングポーリング

learning.reason: Long polling returns a response if a message is found within the maximum wait time. It reduces empty receives without always waiting for the full configured duration.
learning.concept: The polling wait time is how long to wait for a message before receiving it. The visibility timeout is how long to hide a message from other workers after it has been received.

sourceLabel: Amazon SQS — Short and Long Polling

title: Write many small S3 objects concurrently
prompt: A data collection application creates objects of a few KB individually, and downstream processing also reads each object separately from S3 in the same Region. At the start of a new collection run, a large number of PUT requests suddenly target a specific date prefix, and 503 Slow Down responses occur while S3 scales. The upload source's network is not saturated. Which change distributes sustained writes while retaining individual objects?

choices.text: Only increase concurrency across all workers targeting the same date prefix, and immediately retry 503 responses concurrently.
choices.explanation: This concentrates the same load and retries in the same range; it does not spread writes across prefixes.

choices.text: Under the date, use a hash of the data ID to distribute objects across multiple prefixes and write concurrently. Use backoff for 503 responses.
choices.explanation: This distributes load across multiple prefixes while retaining individual object keys and avoids concentrating retries during scaling.

choices.text: Use multipart uploads for each object of a few KB under the same prefix, further dividing each transfer into smaller parts.
choices.explanation: This does not distribute the concentration of PUT requests for small, individual objects across multiple prefixes.

choices.text: Keep the same key structure and use S3 Transfer Acceleration to route traffic from within the Region through an edge location.
choices.explanation: This feature improves transfer paths over long distances; it does not split writes concentrated on the same destination prefix.

source.label: Amazon S3 — パフォーマンスの最適化

learning.reason: Add information to the keys that distributes them across multiple prefixes, and have the relevant workers write concurrently. Retry transient 503 responses with backoff.
learning.concept: S3 scales across partitioned prefixes. Scaling occurs gradually, so a sudden increase in request volume may require handling 503 responses.

title: Balance uneven NLB target counts across Availability Zones
prompt: An internal TCP application is exposed through a Network Load Balancer in two AZs. Each AZ receives roughly the same number of new connections at its NLB node, but one AZ has three healthy targets of equal capacity and the other has nine. Cross-zone load balancing is currently disabled for both the NLB and target group, and each target in the three-target AZ has a higher load. Which change applies if the application placement must be preserved and cross-AZ traffic is allowed?

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing only on the load balancer, and leave it explicitly disabled on the target group.
choices.explanation: The target group's explicit setting takes precedence, so traffic for this group remains limited to targets in the same AZ.

choices.text: Keep it disabled on the target group and increase the health check frequency for targets in the three-target AZ.
choices.explanation: Changing how often target health is evaluated does not let each NLB node select targets in another AZ.

choices.text: Only shorten the socket timeout for targets in the three-target AZ.
choices.explanation: This may change how long individual connections remain open, but it does not distribute new connections from each node across all targets in both AZs.

choices.text: Enable cross-zone load balancing for the target group.
choices.explanation: Both NLB nodes can distribute connections to healthy targets in both AZs, reducing the concentration of load on the three-target AZ.

source.label: Elastic Load Balancing — NLBターゲットグループの属性

learning.reason: When cross-zone load balancing is enabled for the target group, each NLB node can select healthy targets regardless of the AZ in which the node is located.
learning.concept: With cross-zone load balancing disabled, each node distributes traffic only to targets in its own AZ. The target group's setting can override the load balancer's setting.

sourceLabel: Elastic Load Balancing — NLB Target Group Attributes

title: Provide EFS throughput when normal and burst demand differ sharply
prompt: Several EC2 build workers use an existing EFS file system. They spend long periods idle, but read and write many binaries during sudden releases. Average throughput is less than 5% of peak, and the workload has run short of burst credits. Which configuration preserves shared files and adapts to changing demand without setting peak capacity in advance?

choices.text: Change EFS to Elastic Throughput.
choices.explanation: Throughput adjusts to workload demand without being fixed according to total file-system size or burst credits.

choices.text: Change EFS to Provisioned Throughput sized for normal demand.
choices.explanation: This removes reliance on burst credits, but a fixed low throughput cannot keep up with sudden spikes.

choices.text: Keep EFS on Bursting Throughput and move files that are not accessed to IA.
choices.explanation: Changing the storage class does not switch to Elastic Throughput or flexibly increase the burst credits available during spikes.

choices.text: Keep all workers using the same EFS file system and increase only the throughput of each worker's EBS volume.
choices.explanation: Remote reads and writes to EFS are the bottleneck, so faster block storage on each worker does not solve the problem.

source.label: Amazon EFS — スループットモード
