choices.explanation: An SCP controls principals in the targeted member accounts. It does not limit the permissions of a principal from another organization that accesses a bucket directly.

choices.text: Apply an RCP to the audit OU that denies unencrypted connections to the targeted S3 resources.
choices.explanation: The condition can be applied on the resource side, so external roles are also subject to the deny condition.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to make external permissions visible and expect its findings to automatically deny requests that do not use HTTPS.
choices.explanation: Access Analyzer provides visibility; a separate policy is needed to deny requests during authorization.

choices.text: Attach permissions boundaries to internal operator roles in each account and expect them to apply to external partner roles.
choices.explanation: A permissions boundary controls the IAM entity to which it is attached. It does not extend to roles outside your organization.

source.label: AWS Organizations — SCPとRCPで制御できる対象

learning.reason: Apply an RCP to the audit OU to deny unencrypted connections for protected S3 operations. Because it sets a resource-side limit, the condition can also apply to an external role that otherwise has valid permissions.
learning.concept: An SCP controls principals in the targeted accounts within an organization. An RCP controls resource-side access conditions for supported services. An RCP does not grant access by itself, so appropriate existing permissions are still required for HTTPS connections.

sourceLabel: AWS Organizations — What SCPs and RCPs Can Control

title: Cache Lambda authorization results separately for each route
prompt: Multiple routes in an API Gateway HTTP API use the same Lambda authorizer. The authorizer validates the input token and the target route, then returns a simple allow or deny response. The same token can be allowed for one operation and denied for another. Which setting should be changed to keep the token authentication method and simple responses, use caching, and make each route's decision independent?

choices.text: Use only the Authorization header as the identity source and shorten the cache TTL.
choices.explanation: This shortens the reuse period, but during that time the same result could still be used for another route with the same token.

choices.text: Remove the Authorization header and use only $context.routeKey as the identity source.
choices.explanation: This separates routes, but the cache cannot distinguish different authentication tokens used on the same route.

choices.text: Disable the authorizer cache and evaluate every request.
choices.explanation: Each request can be checked independently, but this does not meet the requirement to reuse valid results through caching.

choices.text: Set both the existing Authorization header and $context.routeKey as the authorizer's identity sources.
choices.explanation: This limits reuse of a result to requests with the same token and the same route.

source.label: Amazon API Gateway — HTTP APIのLambda認可とキャッシュ

learning.reason: Keep the existing Authorization header and add $context.routeKey as an authorizer identity source. A cached authorization result is reused only when both the token and route match.
learning.concept: A simple response returns the same decision for requests with the same cache key. Identity sources determine the authorization cache key and are independent of HTTP integration or CDN cache conditions.

sourceLabel: Amazon API Gateway — Lambda authorizer and caching for HTTP APIs

title: Restrict Lambda Function URL access to CloudFront
prompt: General users should use only GET requests to a Lambda function URL through a specific CloudFront distribution. Do not provide AWS credentials to users, and do not allow direct access to the function URL. How should a new function URL and CloudFront origin be configured?

choices.text: Set the function URL to NONE and enable only origin request signing with OAC.
choices.explanation: A function URL configured without authentication cannot restrict callers by IAM, and it does not meet OAC's prerequisites.

choices.text: Set the function URL to AWS_IAM and use OAC without signing. Forward general users' requests as-is.
choices.explanation: An origin configuration that does not sign requests cannot satisfy IAM authentication for general users who have no AWS credentials.

choices.text: Set the function URL to AWS_IAM and configure CloudFront OAC to always sign. In the function policy, limit CloudFront invoke permission to the target distribution.
choices.explanation: This allows CloudFront-to-origin requests to be authenticated and authorized with IAM without requiring credentials from viewers.

choices.text: Set the function URL to AWS_IAM and sign with OAC, but allow CloudFront without restricting access to a specific distribution.
choices.explanation: This does not restrict access to the specified distribution.

source.label: CloudFront: OAC for Lambda Function URLs

learning.reason: Set the function URL to AWS_IAM, configure OAC to always sign, and scope the function-side policy to the CloudFront service principal and the target distribution ARN.
learning.concept: For a new function URL, CloudFront needs both lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl and lambda:InvokeFunction permissions.

sourceLabel: CloudFront: OAC for Lambda Function URLs

title: Let AWS manage RDS master credentials
prompt: Create a new supported RDS for PostgreSQL instance. You want RDS to generate the master password, store it in Secrets Manager, and rotate it periodically, without requiring operators to provide the password or add a rotation function or management application code. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Store the password in an environment variable in the task definition
choices.explanation: This places a long-lived secret in application configuration.

choices.text: Enable Manage master credentials in AWS Secrets Manager
choices.explanation: RDS can manage master credentials in Secrets Manager.

choices.text: Enable storage encryption only
choices.explanation: This does not generate or rotate the password.

choices.text: Enable IAM database authentication only
choices.explanation: This is separate from the RDS-managed master secret setting.

source.label: Amazon RDS: master credentials

learning.reason: The RDS integration with Secrets Manager lets AWS manage the master credentials.
learning.concept: Minimize retrieval permissions and keep the application authentication design separate.

title: Make ECR release tags immutable while allowing development tags to change
prompt: In ECR, tags beginning with release- must not be overwritten, while tags beginning with dev- must be allowed to change across repeated builds. Which repository configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Set all tags to MUTABLE
choices.explanation: Release tags could also be overwritten.

choices.text: Set all tags to IMMUTABLE
choices.explanation: Development tags could no longer be updated across repeated builds.

choices.text: Set tag mutability to IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION and add dev-* as an exclusion filter
choices.explanation: Tags outside the exclusion filter remain immutable, while development tags can be updated. The required setting is IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION.

choices.text: Configure only a lifecycle policy
choices.explanation: A lifecycle policy controls retention and deletion; it does not control whether tags can be overwritten.

source.label: Amazon ECR: tag mutability

learning.reason: IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION allows only excluded tags to remain mutable.
learning.concept: Separate protection against overwriting release tags from the ability to iterate on development builds.

title: Use an ACM-issued public certificate outside AWS
prompt: You need to use an ACM-issued public certificate with both AWS services and servers outside AWS. The private key must be exportable. Which certificate type is most appropriate?

choices.text: Create a standard ACM public certificate
choices.explanation: The private key for a standard ACM-issued public certificate cannot be exported.

choices.text: Use an ACM Private CA certificate on a public server
choices.explanation: A Private CA does not ordinarily issue public certificates trusted by public clients.

choices.text: Only associate the certificate with CloudFront
choices.explanation: Associating the certificate does not provide its private key to an external server.

choices.text: Explicitly select an ACM exportable public certificate
choices.explanation: An exportable ACM public certificate lets you export the certificate and private key for use outside AWS.

source.label: AWS Certificate Manager: exportable public certificates

learning.reason: Selecting an exportable public certificate is an explicit opt-in that allows its private key to be exported for use outside AWS.
learning.concept: Plan how to protect the exported private key and manage certificate renewal.

sourceLabel: AWS Certificate Manager: exportable public certificates

title: Distribute fixed read connections across Valkey replicas
prompt: ElastiCache for Valkey is running in cluster mode disabled configuration, with one primary and three read replicas. The service can tolerate briefly stale cached values and uses the reader endpoint for reads, but the entire application shares one persistent TCP connection, leaving a single replica under heavy load. Without changing the keys or cluster mode, which change will distribute read traffic across multiple replicas?

choices.text: Open multiple read connections to the reader endpoint and distribute the load using a connection pool that appropriately re-resolves DNS.
choices.explanation: This allows new connections to use different replicas and avoids pinning all reads to a single TCP connection.

choices.text: Add replicas but continue to use the same pinned read TCP connection.
choices.explanation: Additional replicas may be used by new name resolutions or connections, but they do not redistribute an existing TCP connection among replicas.

choices.text: Point read connections to the primary endpoint and add more replicas at the same time.
choices.explanation: Connections to the primary do not distribute load to the added read replicas.

choices.text: Keep the reader endpoint and increase only command pipelining over the same TCP connection.
choices.explanation: This can combine network round trips, but it does not change the concentration of load on the endpoint of that single connection.

source.label: Amazon ElastiCache — クラスターモード無効のエンドポイント

learning.reason: The reader endpoint returns replica IP addresses through DNS. A single connection remains attached to the replica it reached, so use multiple connections and name resolutions.
learning.concept: The DNS reader endpoint is not a load balancer that routes each command. Actual distribution also depends on DNS caching and connection reuse.

sourceLabel: Amazon ElastiCache — endpoints for cluster mode disabled

title: Increase FSx disk IOPS while keeping SSD capacity unchanged
prompt: An existing FSx for Windows File Server uses SSD storage. Measurements of random I/O from an SMB application show that it has reached the disk IOPS limit. The file server's throughput capacity supports the desired IOPS, and CPU and network capacity are also available. Storage capacity is sufficient and must remain unchanged. How can you increase only storage IOPS?

choices.text: Keep automatic SSD IOPS configuration and change the maintenance window without changing capacity.
choices.explanation: The storage capacity determines the IOPS under automatic configuration, and maintenance settings cannot increase them.

choices.text: Switch SSD IOPS to user-provisioned mode and specify the required IOPS within the supported range.
choices.explanation: This can increase SSD disk IOPS independently while keeping the existing SSD capacity unchanged.

choices.text: Keep the current SSD IOPS and increase only the file server's throughput capacity.
choices.explanation: The file server has sufficient capacity in this scenario, and this option does not change the IOPS allocated to the bottleneck SSD.

choices.text: Keep automatic IOPS configuration and increase SSD capacity by the amount needed for the IOPS.
choices.explanation: Automatic IOPS increase with capacity, but this violates the requirement to keep storage capacity unchanged.

source.label: Amazon FSx — WindowsファイルシステムのSSD IOPS

learning.reason: User-provisioned SSD IOPS can be configured independently of storage capacity.
learning.concept: The supported maximum depends on capacity and throughput capacity. Distinguish storage capacity and file-server performance from the disk IOPS limit.

sourceLabel: Amazon FSx — SSD IOPS for Windows file systems

title: Choose a Fargate size that meets measured CPU and memory requirements
prompt: A Linux Fargate task will run two containers. Measurements show that the task as a whole needs at least 1.5 vCPU and 9 GiB of memory. Choose a task size from the supported combinations, without provisioning more CPU or memory than necessary. Which task definition is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the task to 1 vCPU and 9 GiB.
choices.explanation: 1 vCPU is below the requirement, and 9 GiB of memory is not available with this CPU size.

choices.text: Set the task to 1.5 vCPU and 9 GiB.
choices.explanation: These values express the requirement, but Fargate does not support specifying 1.5 vCPU for a task.

choices.text: Set the task to 2 vCPU and 9 GiB.
choices.explanation: This meets the CPU and memory requirements and is the smallest combination allowed by Fargate.

choices.text: Set the task to 4 vCPU and 9 GiB.
choices.explanation: This is a valid combination, but it provisions more CPU than necessary because 2 vCPU meets the requirement.

source.label: Amazon ECS — Fargateタスクの有効なCPUとメモリの組み合わせ

learning.reason: Fargate CPU sizes are discrete, and the smallest supported value at or above 1.5 vCPU is 2 vCPU. With 2 vCPU, memory can be configured from 4 to 16 GiB in 1 GiB increments, so 9 GiB is available.
learning.concept: For Fargate, choose a supported combination of CPU and memory for the task as a whole. Configuring resources at the container level does not make an unsupported task size valid.

sourceLabel: Amazon ECS — Valid CPU and memory combinations for Fargate tasks

title: Parallelize Lambda batch processing while keeping the Kinesis shard count unchanged
prompt: Lambda processes records from Kinesis. Shard read and write capacity is available, and the Lambda concurrency quota is sufficient, but currently only one batch per shard is processed at a time and IteratorAge is increasing. Each shard has multiple partition keys, and the records are not aggregated. How can you process records for different keys in parallel while preserving order for the same key, without splitting the stream?

choices.text: Leave the event source mapping's parallelization unchanged and only increase the function's reserved concurrency.
choices.explanation: This increases the concurrency available to the function but does not change the batch parallelization setting within a shard.

choices.text: Enable enhanced fan-out but keep ParallelizationFactor at 1.
choices.explanation: This can provide separate read throughput, but it does not increase the number of batches processed concurrently from one shard.

choices.text: Increase the maximum batching window so that batches can accumulate for longer in each shard.
choices.explanation: This changes how records accumulate; it does not configure parallel batch processing within the same shard.

choices.text: Increase the event source mapping's ParallelizationFactor and monitor IteratorAge.
choices.explanation: This parallelizes processing within existing shards while preserving order for each partition key.

source.label: AWS Lambda — Kinesisのシャード内のバッチ処理

learning.reason: Set the event source mapping's ParallelizationFactor to greater than 1. This processes multiple batches in parallel within a shard while preserving order for each partition key.
learning.concept: Splitting shards to distribute writes and enabling enhanced fan-out to separate consumer read throughput are different measures. The constraint in this question is batch-processing parallelism.

sourceLabel: AWS Lambda — Processing batches within a Kinesis shard

title: Combine measurements from each worker to calculate the overall p99 in CloudWatch
prompt: Multiple workers measure the processing time of the same API in milliseconds. All durations are nonnegative, and there are no more than 150 distinct observed values per worker per minute. Per-caller dimensions are not needed. Each worker should send its observations in aggregated form, and the p99 of all observations should be displayed for the same CloudWatch metric. Which submission format is appropriate?

choices.text: Each worker sends only the minimum, maximum, sum, and sample count for one minute using StatisticValues.
choices.explanation: For samples that generally have different values, this loses the distribution, so the overall p99 cannot be calculated.

choices.text: For the same metric and period, send the observed values and the count of each occurrence in Values and Counts, then display p99 in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This retains how often each value occurred, allowing percentiles for the same metric to be calculated across workers.

choices.text: Each worker sends its calculated p99 as a single value, and the average of those values is treated as the overall p99.
choices.explanation: Averaging individual p99 values does not represent the rank in the distribution formed by combining the original observations.

choices.text: Each worker sends its average and sample count, and all averages are weighted by sample count.
choices.explanation: This calculates the overall average, but averages alone cannot recover the boundary of the top 1%.

source.label: Amazon CloudWatch — PutMetricDataとパーセンタイル

learning.reason: Specify each value actually observed during the period in Values, along with its corresponding occurrence count in Counts. This preserves distribution information for the same metric and lets CloudWatch calculate p99.
learning.concept: Minimum, maximum, sum, and count generally cannot reconstruct a distribution. Values and Counts can preserve the distribution while reducing the amount of data sent when observations are discrete.

title: Reduce connection-establishment overhead with a connection pool for Amazon MQ
prompt: An API using Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ reconnects to the broker each time the same long-lived worker sends a notification. Message transmission itself is fast, but repeatedly opening new connections is the main source of latency. Which improvement preserves how completion of each message send is handled and does not change the broker size?

choices.text: Use the broker's failover transport, but have the application create a new physical connection for every send.
choices.explanation: This helps reconnect to another broker, but it does not reuse connections during normal operation.

choices.text: Keep the existing send logic and increase the consumer's prefetch limit in the application.
choices.explanation: This changes the amount of data retrieved by the consumer. It does not reduce the connections established before sending.

choices.text: Use an ActiveMQ connection pool in the application to reuse physical connections to the broker between sends.
choices.explanation: This avoids establishing a connection for every send while preserving the same broker and message-sending contract.

choices.text: Raise the monitoring threshold, increase the number of connections open at once, and disconnect after each message.
choices.explanation: Increasing parallelism still leaves each send requiring a connection to be established and closed.

source.label: Amazon MQ — ActiveMQのコネクションプール

learning.reason: Reuse physical connections in long-lived workers to reduce short-lived connection activity at the broker.
learning.concept: Pooling and failover transport serve different purposes. Configure reuse for normal operation and switching over during failures separately.

title: Automatically scale RDS storage up to a limit as usage grows over time
prompt: Data usage on a supported Amazon RDS DB instance increases over periods of several weeks without notice. The DB class and I/O performance meet the requirements and do not need to change. There is ample headroom now, so do not provision extra storage based on a maximum estimate up front; instead, automatically increase allocated storage up to a specified limit as free space decreases. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Increase the RDS DB instance class while keeping the same storage allocation.
choices.explanation: This increases compute capacity but does not increase storage based on available free space.

choices.text: Do not use storage autoscaling; allocate the maximum expected capacity up front.
choices.explanation: This provisions capacity in advance and does not meet the requirement to adjust allocated storage as usage grows.

choices.text: Keep the same storage allocation and increase only the Provisioned IOPS setting.
choices.explanation: This changes disk performance, not the amount of data the storage can hold.

choices.text: Enable RDS storage autoscaling and set the required maximum storage threshold.
choices.explanation: This can increase the allocated storage of an existing instance within the specified limit when the applicable conditions are met.

source.label: Amazon RDS — ストレージ自動スケーリング

learning.reason: Set a maximum threshold with storage autoscaling so allocated storage can increase as needed.
learning.concept: Autoscaling has free-space thresholds and processing intervals, so it cannot always outpace a large bulk load. This feature does not automatically reduce storage that has already been allocated.

title: Drain existing TCP connections after an NLB marks a target unhealthy
prompt: Change the behavior of a TCP NLB with multiple healthy targets when one target temporarily fails health checks. Stop sending new connections to that target and allow a 60-second draining period for existing TCP connections. Keep the target registered, and allow it to recover health during the period. How should you configure this?

choices.text: Keep unhealthy connection termination enabled and set the deregistration delay to 60 seconds.
choices.explanation: No deregistration is taking place. Existing connections to a target marked unhealthy follow the immediate termination setting when it is enabled.

choices.text: Disable unhealthy connection termination and set the unhealthy target draining interval to 60 seconds.
choices.explanation: This stops new connections to the unhealthy target and allows existing connections to remain during the specified draining period.

choices.text: Disable unhealthy connection termination but set only the deregistration delay to 60 seconds.
choices.explanation: This can prevent immediate connection termination, but a different attribute controls the 60-second draining state for an unhealthy target.

choices.text: Increase the health check failure threshold and treat the target as healthy until 60 seconds have passed.
choices.explanation: New connections might still be sent to the target before it is marked unhealthy. This also does not configure draining for existing connections after that point.

source.label: Network Load Balancer target group attributes

learning.reason: Disable connection termination for unhealthy targets, then configure the unhealthy target draining interval.
learning.concept: Deregistration draining starts through a separate operation. If health recovers during draining for an unhealthy target, the target can return to a healthy state.

sourceLabel: Network Load Balancer target group attributes

title: Update a secret independently in the recovery Region
prompt: A Secrets Manager secret is replicated from the production Region to a recovery Region. After a disruption makes the production Region unavailable, the recovery-side application starts with the copied value. The recovery-side database has been promoted, and its credentials must be updated independently in the recovery Region. Which operation is required to keep using the existing replica?

choices.text: Change the replica's KMS key to a key in the recovery Region, then update its value while keeping the replication relationship.
choices.explanation: Changing the replica's key does not grant the ability or change the state needed to update its value independently.

choices.text: Configure rotation on the production-side secret and assume that the value will be reflected only in the running recovery Region.
choices.explanation: The production side is unavailable, and a replica that remains in a replication relationship cannot be edited independently of production.

choices.text: Promote the replica to a standalone secret in the recovery Region, then update the credentials there.
choices.explanation: This allows the value to be updated without depending on production and lets recovery operations continue using the existing replica as their basis.

choices.text: Have the application retrieve AWSPREVIOUS and expect the replica to become the primary automatically during the next rotation.
choices.explanation: Specifying a version stage does not change the replication relationship or whether the replica can be updated.

source.label: AWS Secrets Manager — レプリカのスタンドアロンへの昇格

learning.reason: Promote the replica to a standalone secret in the recovery Region, then verify that the recovery application and rotation configuration use that Region's secret and database.
learning.concept: Promotion breaks replication with the production secret. Before promotion, the independent replica setting that can be changed is its encryption key; the secret value itself requires independence before it can be updated.

sourceLabel: AWS Secrets Manager — Promoting a replica to a standalone secret

title: Keep old resources during alarm monitoring after a CloudFormation update
prompt: A CloudFormation stack update replaces multiple resources. A CloudWatch alarm already exists, and after the new resources are deployed, you want an alarm to automatically roll back the entire stack update if it enters ALARM during a 20-minute period. If there are no issues, clean up the old resources through the normal process after the 20-minute monitoring period ends. What should you configure?

choices.text: Set the alarm as a rollback trigger and set the monitoring period to 0 minutes.
choices.explanation: The alarm is monitored during deployment, but there is no 20-minute grace period afterward, so cleanup of the old resources can begin if no issue occurs.

choices.text: Register the existing CloudWatch alarm as a rollback trigger and set the monitoring period to 20 minutes.
choices.explanation: If the alarm enters ALARM during the post-deployment grace period, the update is rolled back. If there is no issue, cleanup of the old resources begins after the period ends.

choices.text: Set only the monitoring period to 20 minutes without registering the alarm ARN as a rollback trigger.
choices.explanation: This can delay cleanup, but the alarm is not associated with the update to trigger an automatic rollback.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain for each resource and use the alarm only for notifications.
choices.explanation: The old resources may be retained, but the alarm will not automatically roll back the entire stack, and the normal cleanup will not run after monitoring ends.

source.label: AWS CloudFormation — ロールバックトリガーと監視時間

learning.reason: Specify the alarm as a rollback trigger and set the monitoring period to 20 minutes. CloudFormation monitors during and after deployment and rolls back the update if the alarm enters ALARM during the period.
learning.concept: An alarm is monitored during deployment even when the monitoring period is 0. Specify a positive monitoring period to provide a post-deployment grace period and delay cleanup of old resources.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudFormation — Rollback triggers and monitoring period

title: Accepting Different Customers’ Notifications Separately in FIFO with the Same Deduplication ID
prompt: An SQS FIFO queue uses a different MessageGroupId for each customer and uses the order number within each customer’s data as the MessageDeduplicationId. Because order numbers are assigned per customer, the same order number can exist for different customers. How can the queue independently accept orders from different customers that have the same order number during the deduplication interval, while preserving the producer’s numbering and order within each customer?

choices.text: Keep the deduplication scope at the queue level and shorten the receive visibility timeout.
choices.explanation: Visibility affects redelivery after a message is received. It does not change the scope in which the same deduplication ID is evaluated when sending.

choices.text: Use the same MessageGroupId for all customers and set the deduplication scope to the message group.
choices.explanation: Putting all messages in the same group does not separate different customers with the same order number from deduplication.

choices.text: Leave the deduplication scope unchanged and add content-based deduplication while continuing to send the explicit order number.
choices.explanation: An explicit deduplication ID takes precedence, so the same order number from different customers cannot be distinguished without changing the scope.

choices.text: Keep a separate MessageGroupId for each customer and set the queue’s deduplication scope to the message group.
choices.explanation: This preserves ordering per customer and limits duplicate evaluation to the same customer’s group.

source.label: Amazon SQS — FIFOの重複排除スコープ

learning.reason: Set the queue’s deduplication scope to the message group. A repeated order number within the group representing a customer is suppressed, while the same number in another group is treated as an independent notification.
learning.concept: Whether deduplication is applied at the queue level or message-group level determines the scope in which the same ID is evaluated. This is separate from ordering by group ID and from making each operation’s side effects idempotent.

title: Preventing Accidental API Stops of a Critical Standalone EC2 Instance
prompt: A critical standalone EC2 instance uses EBS as its root volume. Authorized operators have permission to modify the instance, but you do not want an accidental stop through a normal console or API operation to stop it. For a planned stop, protection will be explicitly removed first. Shutdown control from within the OS is managed separately. Which feature should be enabled?

choices.text: Enable DisableApiStop and disable it through the approved procedure before a planned stop.
choices.explanation: This prevents accidental stops through normal EC2 operations and allows a planned stop after protection is removed.

choices.text: Enable only DisableApiTermination, which also rejects stop requests.
choices.explanation: Termination protection alone does not reject normal stop requests.

choices.text: Change InstanceInitiatedShutdownBehavior to stop.
choices.explanation: This setting determines what happens when a shutdown is initiated from within the OS; it does not control the result of a stop from the EC2 API.

choices.text: Disable DeleteOnTermination for the root EBS volume.
choices.explanation: This setting retains the volume when the instance is terminated; it does not prevent the instance from being stopped.

source.label: Amazon EC2 — APIによる停止の保護

learning.reason: Enable stop protection by setting DisableApiStop. It protects the instance from normal stop operations through the EC2 console, CLI, and API.
learning.concept: Termination protection and stop protection apply to different operations. API stop protection does not apply to shutdowns initiated from within the OS.

title: Recovering a Server to a Healthy Point Before Data Corruption Was Replicated
prompt: An on-premises server is continuously replicated with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery. The operations team has identified when logical storage corruption began, and the latest recovery snapshot contains the corruption. A recoverable point from just before the corruption is still available on the recovery side. Which operation is appropriate to resume service on the recovery side?

choices.text: Launch a recovery instance with the latest data and assume that corrupted blocks will automatically be excluded from synchronization at boot.
choices.explanation: Storage replication does not determine whether business data is healthy and remove corrupted data from the latest recovery point.

choices.text: Launch the recovery side with the latest data, then fail back to on premises and assume it will return to the state before corruption.
choices.explanation: Failback is an operation for returning changes made on the recovery side; it is not a way to select a snapshot from before the corruption.

choices.text: When launching the recovery instance, select a snapshot from a specific point in time before the corruption.
choices.explanation: You can select an available recovery point that does not contain the corrupted data.

choices.text: Create a recovery instance with the latest data, then restore an earlier point in time simply by rebooting that instance.
choices.explanation: A normal reboot cannot restore storage to an earlier recovery point.

source.label: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery — 復旧インスタンスの起動時点

learning.reason: When launching the recovery instance, select a snapshot from a specific point in time before the corruption. Use a state confirmed to predate the corruption rather than the latest replicated data.
learning.concept: Continuous replication copies storage changes from the source, so logical corruption may be present in the latest data. Determine the time using observed recovery points and data validation.

sourceLabel: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery — Recovery Instance Launch Point

title: Recording Expired Lambda Events in a Failure Destination Without Processing Them
prompt: A system directly invokes Lambda asynchronously. After 10 minutes from acceptance, an event no longer has business value. During periods of congestion, events can wait in the internal queue before the function runs. You want events that expire after acceptance or continue to fail during execution to be recorded in a separate SQS queue for investigation. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Set the function timeout to 600 seconds and leave the maximum age of asynchronous events at its default.
choices.explanation: This only limits processing time after execution starts; it does not discard events that spend more than 10 minutes in the internal queue.

choices.text: Set the maximum age of asynchronous events to 600 seconds and configure a standard SQS queue as the failure destination.
choices.explanation: Events that exceed their validity period in the internal queue, as well as invocations that fail after retries, can be sent to the designated destination for recording.

choices.text: Set only the maximum retry attempts to 0 and do not configure a failure destination.
choices.explanation: This can prevent retries after a function error, but it does not set an expiration for events waiting before their first invocation or provide an investigation record.

choices.text: Set the sender’s HTTP timeout to 600 seconds and leave Lambda’s asynchronous settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: An asynchronous invocation returns an acceptance response. The client’s connection wait time cannot control the expiration of an event in the queue after acceptance.

source.label: AWS Lambda — 非同期呼び出しのエラー処理とイベントの期限

learning.reason: Set the maximum event age to 600 seconds in the asynchronous configuration and use a standard SQS queue as the failure destination. This retains records of expired events or invocations that exhaust their retries.
learning.concept: The function timeout limits execution after it starts. The maximum event age for asynchronous invocation sets how long an event can wait in Lambda’s internal queue. The function should also enforce strict business-time constraints.

sourceLabel: AWS Lambda — Asynchronous Invocation Error Handling and Event Expiration

title: Keep existing regional connections open during maintenance with Global Accelerator
prompt: A single standard Global Accelerator has healthy endpoint groups in two Regions. To perform maintenance in Region A, you need to stop new connections from going to A and direct them to B, while allowing the TCP connections still active in A to finish as each client completes them. Keep the public static IP addresses and health checks unchanged. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Delete the listener, wait for existing connections in A to finish, and then recreate the same listener with only B.
choices.explanation: This does not stop only new connections to A; it affects acceptance across the accelerator and its existing use.

choices.text: Intentionally fail the health check in Region A and suspend normal monitoring until maintenance is complete.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to leave health checks unchanged. A traffic dial can suppress only new connections to the Region under maintenance.

choices.text: Set Region A’s traffic dial to 50 and preserve existing connections.
choices.explanation: Existing connections are preserved, but A remains a candidate for new connections.

choices.text: Set Region A’s traffic dial to 0 on the existing accelerator and keep B healthy.
choices.explanation: New connections are directed to another Region, and this setting change does not disconnect connections already in progress.

source.label: AWS Global Accelerator — リージョンへのトラフィックダイヤル

learning.reason: Set the traffic dial for Region A’s endpoint group to 0 and keep B healthy. The change applies to new connections; existing connections and health checks remain in place.
learning.concept: The dial applies to connections directed to a regional endpoint group. It acts at a different level from weights, which adjust the distribution among multiple endpoints within a group.

sourceLabel: AWS Global Accelerator — Traffic Dials for Regions

title: Encrypt specified form fields from CloudFront to the payment service
prompt: A web application receives URL-encoded payment forms over HTTPS through CloudFront. The origin supports chunked transfer. A relay application needs to read fields such as the shipping destination, but only a separate payment service should be able to read the designated payment data fields. How can you encrypt those fields before they reach the origin without changing browser code?

choices.text: Use HTTPS from CloudFront to the origin and forward the form contents unchanged.
choices.explanation: This protects the connection, but once TLS terminates at the origin, it does not restrict which fields the relay application can see.

choices.text: Encrypt the origin’s storage with SSE-KMS and let the relay application process the received form as usual.
choices.explanation: This protects data at rest but does not encrypt specified fields in the request body before it reaches the origin.

choices.text: Associate CloudFront field-level encryption with the cache behavior. Configure the fields to encrypt and a public key, and keep the private key only in the payment service.
choices.explanation: The specified fields remain encrypted at the origin, and only the service with the private key can decrypt them.

choices.text: Authorize users with CloudFront signed cookies and forward the payment form body unchanged.
choices.explanation: This controls who can access the content; it does not encrypt form fields to hide them from the relay application.

source.label: Amazon CloudFront: field-level encryption

learning.reason: Use CloudFront to encrypt the specified fields with the payment service’s public key, and keep the private key only in the payment service.
learning.concept: Check that the form format is supported, the origin supports chunked transfer, and the behavior uses HTTPS.

title: Observe matches for individual AWS WAF managed rules on the same request
prompt: Add a new AWS WAF managed rule group to a web ACL. During the evaluation period, you want to prevent this group from blocking requests and observe the count for every matching rule. If one request matches multiple rules, the evaluation must not stop at the first rule that could block it. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Override only the action returned by the rule group to Count, without changing its internal rules.
choices.explanation: This prevents blocking based on the returned result, but evaluation within the group still stops when the first terminating rule matches.

choices.text: Create a broadly matching Allow rule before the managed rule group.
choices.explanation: Because Allow is terminating, evaluation never reaches the managed rule group, so you cannot observe the counts for individual rules.

choices.text: Enable only sampled request display for the group and leave each rule’s action unchanged.
choices.explanation: Enabling an observation feature does not change existing terminating actions, so the group can still block requests.

choices.text: Override each rule’s action in the added group to Count.
choices.explanation: Each match becomes nonterminating, so evaluation continues to later rules in the managed rule group.

source.label: AWS WAF — ルール単位とルールグループのアクション上書き

learning.reason: Use a per-rule override to set Count. Overriding only the action returned by the rule group does not change the evaluation order inside it.
learning.concept: Before rollout, review per-rule counts and then choose the actions to use in production.

sourceLabel: AWS WAF — Rule-level and rule group action overrides

title: Apply the account-level public access block to an S3 access point policy
prompt: An S3 bucket and an internet-accessible access point are in the same AWS account. When the access point was created, its individual public access block was explicitly disabled, and BlockPublicPolicy is also disabled for the bucket, but BlockPublicPolicy is enabled at the account level. Assume there are no additional restrictions from an organization policy or IAM permissions. What does S3 do when a new access point policy that allows anyone to read is saved?

choices.text: The access point’s own setting takes precedence, so the account-level BlockPublicPolicy is ignored and the policy can be saved.
choices.explanation: Disabling the setting on a resource does not relax the account-level restriction.

choices.text: The policy is rejected when saved because account-level BlockPublicPolicy is more restrictive than the access point setting.
choices.explanation: The most restrictive applicable settings take effect, so the new public policy cannot be saved.

choices.text: The policy is saved, but BlockPublicPolicy unconditionally denies access only when someone tries to use it.
choices.explanation: BlockPublicPolicy rejects an attempt to configure a new policy that allows public access.

choices.text: Saving the access point policy is rejected only if BlockPublicAcls is also enabled at the account level.
choices.explanation: Controls for ACLs and controls for new public policies serve different purposes.

source.label: Amazon S3: Block Public Access

learning.reason: Account-level BlockPublicPolicy is enabled, so a less restrictive setting below that level cannot allow the public policy to be saved.
learning.concept: Distinguish rejection of a new public policy from other public access block settings that apply to existing policies or public ACLs.

title: Limit one session of an existing role to read-only access
prompt: An approved operations platform assumes an existing role shared by multiple departments from an external operations account. The role's identity-based policy covers multiple buckets, but only the credentials issued for this request must be limited to GetObject on a specified prefix. The target bucket does not grant access directly to the session, and no permanent policy will be changed. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Set a permissions boundary for this request on the shared role and remove it after maintenance.
choices.explanation: This changes an attribute of the shared role and does not meet the requirement to apply the condition only to this session.

choices.text: Shorten the role's maximum session duration and issue credentials with the same role permissions.
choices.explanation: This changes only the credential lifetime. It does not restrict which buckets or operations can be accessed.

choices.text: Pass a session policy allowing only GetObject on the specified prefix when making the call that issues the approved temporary credentials.
choices.explanation: The session can be restricted to the intersection of the role's identity-based permissions and the session policy.

choices.text: Set the External ID value in AssumeRole to the specified prefix so that S3 uses that string as the access scope.
choices.explanation: An External ID is a condition for assuming a role; it does not directly define the scope of S3 operations for a session.

source.label: AWS IAM — セッションポリシーとテンポラリ認証情報

learning.reason: A session policy supplied when assuming a role with STS retains only a subset of the operations that the existing role permits for that session.
learning.concept: A session policy cannot add operations that the role does not permit.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM — Session policies and temporary credentials

title: Revoke only the compromised certificate
prompt: Several certificates for internal servers, issued by AWS Private CA, are validated by client devices. The private key for one server has been compromised. The affected certificate contains the AWS Private CA OCSP responder URL that was configured at issuance, and clients can check revocation status through OCSP. What should be done to avoid waiting for expiration while continuing to use the other server certificates?

choices.text: Revoke the issuing CA itself and continue using the same chain for the other servers' certificates.
choices.explanation: Removing trust in the issuer would also affect other certificates that use the same chain.

choices.text: Revoke the single affected certificate at the issuing CA and have managed clients check it through OCSP.
choices.explanation: This limits the impact to the affected certificate, and clients can recognize the updated revocation status.

choices.text: Deploy another certificate to the compromised server without revoking the old certificate.
choices.explanation: The deployed certificate changes, but the validity of the compromised old certificate is not revoked.

choices.text: Delete only the affected certificate's public key from the server and leave the clients' validation method unchanged.
choices.explanation: The server's state does not change the validity period of an issued certificate or the CA's revocation information.

source.label: AWS Private CA — 証明書の失効と状態確認

learning.reason: Revoke the affected end-entity certificate at the issuing CA and continue validation through OCSP on clients. Once the revocation is reflected in the response, other valid certificates issued by the same CA can remain in use.
learning.concept: Build revocation checks into client operations. It may take time for OCSP to return new revocation information.

sourceLabel: AWS Private CA — Certificate revocation and status checks

title: Find organization-specific identifiers in existing S3 documents
prompt: An audit team wants to detect an organization-specific contract number in supported-format documents already stored in a particular S3 bucket. The number follows a fixed string pattern, and it should be detected only when a keyword indicating contract management appears nearby. Which method can inspect documents in the specified bucket without operating a custom analysis job?

choices.text: Use only Macie's managed identifiers and add a regular expression matching the contract number to an allow list.
choices.explanation: A managed identifier cannot be extended with a detection pattern. An allow list is used to exclude matching values from results.

choices.text: Export an object listing to S3 Inventory and inspect strings in object names and tags.
choices.explanation: Inventory can show included metadata, but it does not inspect the contents of stored documents.

choices.text: Configure a regular expression and keywords in a Macie custom identifier, then use it in a sensitive data discovery job targeting the specified bucket.
choices.explanation: This detects the target data using a custom pattern and a proximity condition in the document contents.

choices.text: Use IAM Access Analyzer to check whether the bucket is public and exclude objects that are not public from detection.
choices.explanation: Access Analyzer analyzes access permissions; it does not inspect document contents or formats.

source.label: Amazon Macie — カスタムデータ識別子

learning.reason: Define a Macie custom data identifier with a regular expression and keyword proximity criteria, then use it in a sensitive data discovery job targeting the S3 bucket.
learning.concept: Custom data identifiers detect organization-specific patterns. They have a different role from managed identifiers for standard data, allow lists that exclude matching strings from results, and storage metadata for S3 objects.

title: Detect a sudden change in the error rate of management APIs
prompt: An operations team audits management APIs in an AWS account. For recorded write management events, it wants to detect intervals with anomalous activity relative to the normal error rate, without setting a fixed threshold for the number of API errors. The CloudTrail trail records write management events. No custom model will be operated. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable only API call rate analysis in CloudTrail Insights.
choices.explanation: This detects changes in call volume; it does not inspect a rise in the error rate when the number of calls remains the same.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and use the digest to determine deviations in API errors from normal levels.
choices.explanation: A digest provides information to validate log file tampering or loss; it does not analyze anomalous API error rates.

choices.text: Add only S3 object read data events to the same trail.
choices.explanation: This adds events to audit; it does not enable anomaly detection for management API error rates.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail Insights API error rate analysis on the trail and review detection results based on management events.
choices.explanation: This can detect activity that deviates from the normal API error rate without a manually set fixed threshold.

source.label: AWS CloudTrail — InsightsとAPIエラー率

learning.reason: Enable CloudTrail Insights API error rate analysis on the trail. Insights events can be recorded when activity is anomalous relative to the account's normal API error rate.
learning.concept: Recording management events and recording Insights events that indicate anomalies are separate. API call rate analysis targets changes in call volume, while API error rate analysis targets changes in error behavior.

sourceLabel: AWS CloudTrail — Insights and API error rates

title: Protecting an S3 object version under investigation indefinitely
prompt: In a management bucket with versioning and S3 Object Lock enabled, the current and previous versions of records have compliance-mode retention dates. For a specific version under investigation, protection must continue even after that date passes, and only an authorized operator may remove the additional protection when the investigation ends. The existing retention dates cannot be changed. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Place a legal hold on the target version and restrict the permissions needed to place and remove it to authorized operators.
choices.explanation: The retention date remains unchanged, while protection for the target version can continue until the investigation ends.

choices.text: Extend the compliance-mode retention date for the target version to a later date, then restore the original date if the investigation ends early.
choices.explanation: A compliance-mode retention date cannot be shortened. This also violates the requirement not to change the original retention date.

choices.text: Only lengthen the bucket's default retention period and assume that existing target versions will automatically receive protection with no expiration.
choices.explanation: Default retention does not add an indefinite hold to an existing target version.

choices.text: Add a delete marker to the target key and assume the version can no longer be removed from the version listing.
choices.explanation: A delete marker hides the key from ordinary retrieval. It does not control permanent deletion of the target version.

source.label: Amazon S3 — Object Lockのリーガルホールド

learning.reason: Place a legal hold on the version under investigation and restrict the permission to remove it to authorized operators. Because the hold operates separately from the existing fixed retention date, protection can continue after that date expires.
learning.concept: A legal hold has no fixed expiration time. If it is removed before the fixed retention date, the version remains protected for the rest of its retention period.

sourceLabel: Amazon S3 — Object Lock Legal Holds

title: Carrying project attributes into downstream roles for authorization
prompt: A deployment system chains role assumptions from an initial role session to a working role in another account. The downstream working role must allow operations only on resources whose tags match the Project value determined at a trusted starting point. Multiple projects share the same working role, and the project must not be specified again at each step in the chain. Which configuration is needed?

choices.text: Add a Project resource tag to the starting role and assume it will be copied automatically to every role in the assumption chain.
choices.explanation: A resource tag attached to a role does not become a session tag inherited by downstream roles.

choices.text: Pass Project as a regular session tag in the initial assumption without specifying it as transitive.
choices.explanation: It can be evaluated in the first session, but by default it is not carried into subsequent sessions.

choices.text: Pass Project as a session tag at the starting point and designate it as transitive. Allow the tag on the trusted assumption path and evaluate the principal tag downstream.
choices.explanation: This carries the trusted value into multiple role sessions and enables attribute-based authorization with a shared role.

choices.text: Use a different External ID for each project at the starting point and compare the External ID as a principal tag in downstream resource policies.
choices.explanation: An External ID is a condition for role assumption; it is not inherited as a principal tag for downstream resource operations.

source.label: AWS IAM — 連鎖するロールとSTSセッションタグ

learning.reason: Pass Project as a session tag in the initial assumption and designate it as transitive with TransitiveTagKeys. Control TagSession on the required roles, then evaluate the principal's Project tag in the final access permissions.
learning.concept: Session tags are not carried to downstream roles by default. Distinguish resource tags on the role itself from inheritable session attributes passed when assuming a role.

sourceLabel: AWS IAM — Chained Roles and STS Session Tags
